uk_vickers_gbt_155: After the multinational SP70 programme collapsed in the 1980s, VSEL designed the GBT 155: a 155 mm turret built around the FH-70 howitzer that could be fitted to Vickers Mk.3, Chieftain, Centurion or Challenger hulls as a cheap way to upgrade old tanks. It found no buyers, though the design fed into the AS90 and Poland's Krab. In the game it is quick for an artillery vehicle and its big gun reloads briskly, but the tall hull is easy to spot, the turret only keeps out rifle-calibre fire, and the packed ammunition often cooks off when penetrated. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
uk_vickers_mbt_mk_1: Vickers-Armstrongs built this export main battle tank as a private venture in the 1960s, combining the L7 105 mm gun, the Leyland L60 multi-fuel engine and Chieftain fire control and transmission into an affordable package. India adopted it as the licence-built Vijayanta, and Kuwait bought 70 adapted for desert use. In the game it suits a support or sniping role: gun depression is good and an aced crew reloads in five seconds, but the 4.9-6.0x sight limits long-range work, mobility is average and the flat turret front is weak, although the 60-degree hull plate gives moderate protection. It was added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
uk_vickers_mbt_mk_3: The last Vickers tank to win export orders, the Mk.3 reworked the Mk.1 with a cast turret front and mantlet, a Chieftain laser rangefinder in place of the ranging machine gun, and room for 50 rounds; Kenya and Nigeria ordered it in numbers and still field it. Compared with the Mk.1 it has a sturdier turret, 10 degrees of gun depression for hull-down play, a 720 hp engine that slightly improves mobility, and M456 HEAT-FS for targets that defeat APDS, though its sight is fixed at 10x. It arrived in the "Direct Hit" update.
uk_vickers_mk7: A 1980s Vickers prototype, the Mk.7 put a turret with Chobham armour, a proven L11 120 mm gun and good fire control onto a Leopard 2 chassis, which makes it an unusual entry in the British tree. In the game that mix gives a rare balance: the German engine provides real mobility, the turret offers decent protection and the gun hits hard, backed by improved TOGS thermals, a laser rangefinder and smoke launchers. It suits several playstyles and was added in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
uk_vickers_mk_11: Vickers built the Mk.11 privately for an Australian long-range patrol vehicle tender, pairing a Timoney Mark 8 wheeled hull with the turret of the VFM5 light tank prototype; despite plans for APC, SPAA and other versions, only one prototype was made after work began in 1993. In the game it is big and thinly armoured, slow across rough ground but quick on roads, and it carries the familiar L7 gun with a laser rangefinder and can swim. It came with Update 2.31 "Kings of Battle".
uk_vickers_mk_6_aa_mk_1: Built after the fall of France to counter German air raids and dive bombers, this anti-aircraft conversion of the first Vickers Light Tank Mk.VI has a powered one-man turret with four 7.92 mm BESA machine guns. In the game it is extremely fragile, so concealment from both ground vehicles and aircraft matters. Low muzzle velocity and modest damage per hit mean holding fire until a plane is close and expecting to land many rounds, and several aircraft taking turns to strafe are a real danger. It was added in Update 1.79 "Project X".
uk_vijayanta: India's first home-built main battle tank was a licence-made Vickers Mk.1; a prototype reached India in 1964 and the type entered service the following year, fought in the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War, and some were still with border troops as late as 2019. The premium version in the game plays almost exactly like the Mk.1 but adds the M456 105 mm HEAT-FS round. Its armour is poor for its level, so it works best as a support tank kept well away from the front line. It arrived with the "La Royale" update.
uk_ystervark_spaa: South Africa's Ystervark ("porcupine") is a mine-protected anti-aircraft truck of the 1980s, made by taking one of the Project Sireb prototypes, the "Bulldog", and replacing its passenger compartment with a weapons mount. In the game its accurate, rapid-firing 20 mm GAI-C01 cannon brings down aircraft readily, but ammunition is limited, so short bursts are the rule. The crew sit fully exposed, making concealment vital, and HVAP rounds give some anti-tank ability that is best kept for emergencies. It came with the "Ground Breaking" update.
us_adats_bradley: ADATS is a modular dual-role missile system able to engage both aircraft and armoured vehicles; the US Army version sat on an M3 Bradley chassis with a 25 mm cannon and 12.7 mm machine gun added, but budget cuts, post-Cold War priorities and poor bad-weather performance killed it in the early 1990s before fielding. In the game its eight MIM-146 missiles double as anti-tank weapons, with up to 900 mm of penetration and a 6 kg TNT-equivalent warhead. Against aircraft, its 10 km reach can feel short. It was added in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
us_ags_teledyne: Teledyne Continental Motors' early-1980s entry for the Armored Gun System contest, meant to replace the M551 Sheridan, stood out for its unmanned turret; it lost to the CCVL and was later pitched for export. In the game the tiny turret is its great asset: from a good hull-down spot it is very hard to disable, helped by 10 degrees of gun depression. Anything with an autocannon or bigger can tear it apart once the hull is exposed, though, and lingering in one place invites artillery or bombs. It was a reward in the 2021 Operation W.I.N.T.E.R. event, added in "Winged Lions".
us_ccvl: FMC's entry for the Armored Gun System competition to replace the M551 Sheridan used an autoloader to cut the crew to three; it was selected in 1992 and became the M8 AGS, though procurement was terminated in 1997. In the game it combines a soft-recoil, autoloaded 105 mm M68A1 gun with a two-plane stabiliser, laser rangefinder and gunner's thermal sight, plus excellent mobility. Its armour only stops heavy machine gun fire and shell fragments, so it is a fast, hard-hitting light tank rather than a brawler. It was a reward in the 2022 "Overpowered" event, added in "Drone Age".
us_efv_p1: General Dynamics developed the EFV from 1996 to 2011 to replace the US Marine Corps' AAV-7A1, adding a 30 mm Bushmaster and powerful water-jet propulsion, but changing doctrine and high costs led to its cancellation. In the game its huge hull is wrapped in layered composite screens on every side but the front, and the roomy interior lets it absorb hits that miss vital parts. On water it reaches 42 km/h, far quicker than other amphibians. The 30 mm cannon mainly threatens light vehicles or targets caught from the flank, which its bulk makes hard to arrange. It was a 2025 "Semper Fidelis" event reward in "Tusk Force".
us_halftrack_m13: White Motor Company produced the M13 MGMC, the first anti-aircraft version of the M3 half-track, from 1942 to 1943; it saw combat only at Anzio before the four-gun M16 replaced it in 1944. In the game its thin, upright armour offers almost nothing, so it relies on speed, handling and cover. The machine guns can hurt some light tanks, but aircraft should remain the priority, and artillery is a cue to move at once because fragments easily destroy it. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_halftrack_m15: One of the first vehicles in the American ground tree at Update 1.45 "Steel Generals", the M15 CGMC is an anti-aircraft half-track pairing a 37 mm cannon with Browning heavy machine guns. Compared with the machine-gun-only M13 and M16 it has real armour and a cannon that downs aircraft faster at range, but it carries far less ammunition, its mixed weapons are harder to aim, and the mount traverses slowly and cannot fire over the cab. The Brownings only fire on the machine gun key. It works best behind friendly lines with a clear view of the sky, ideally with the guns facing rearward.
us_halftrack_m16: The second anti-aircraft variant of the M3 half-track mounted four M2HB Brownings on an M45 quad mount; White built around 2,700 in 1943-44, and their deadliness against infantry and low-flying planes earned the nickname "Meat Chopper" before the type left US service in 1954. In the game it handles like the M13: too lightly armoured to fight tanks, but its guns set aircraft alight readily, provided it waits until they are near. Moving after each engagement helps it survive. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_halftrack_m3_75mm_gmc: Improvised for the new Tank Destroyer Branch after France fell in 1940, the M3 GMC simply placed a French-designed 75 mm gun on an M3 half-track; up to 2,200 were built from 1941 to 1943 and served in the Pacific, North Africa and Italy before the M10 took over. In the game the half-track body offers little survivability, but the gun hits hard for its rank and can deal with the odd medium or heavy tank at Rank I. The long reload is the catch, so every shot must count and a safe place to reload is essential. It came with Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
us_hstv_l: A late-1970s testbed from the joint Army and Marine Corps ARMVAL programme, the HSTV-L explored whether speed could replace heavy armour as protection; its centrepiece was the ARES XM274, a rapid-firing 75 mm hyper-velocity smoothbore meant to break composite armour with quick follow-up hits. Only one was built, and the Army settled on 105 mm as the minimum calibre for such vehicles. In the game it is a quick, hard-hitting flanker with a stabiliser, laser rangefinder, thermals and an autoloader cycling in as little as 1.5 seconds, plus excellent gun depression, though the small calibre can struggle against some MBTs head-on. It arrived in "Starfighters".
us_lav_ad: Built so the US Marine Corps' fast LAV battalions would have their own short-range air cover, the LAV-AD combined the LAV-25 hull with a rotary cannon plus Stingers; trials began in 1992 and 17 had been delivered by 1997. In the game it has virtually no armour, as even heavy machine guns go through the sides. Stingers work best against aircraft inside about 3 km, often forcing evasion even when they miss, while the gun covers targets too close for the missiles to arm. Swapping the Stingers for rocket pods, alongside HVAP rounds, lets it tackle light vehicles. It arrived in "Wind of Change".
us_losat_ccv: Lockheed Martin's MGM-166 LOSAT destroyed armour by impact energy alone, using an 80 kg missile flying at over Mach 4 that crossed its 4 km range in under four seconds; it was dropped in 2004 over slow reloads, cost, poor close-range results and little use against light targets. In the game it must see its target directly, which exposes it when firing, and the missiles are weak up close but defeat almost anything once at full speed. Lacking gun elevation or depression, it suits big, open maps where its speed can claim long sightlines; its armour is thin. It was a 2023 Tokushu Heiki event reward in "Sons of Attila".
us_lvt_4_zis_2: After capturing many LVT(A)(4) amphibians from the Nationalists in 1949 and losing access to American ammunition, China's People's Liberation Army replaced their 75 mm howitzer turrets with the high-velocity Soviet 57 mm ZiS-2 anti-tank gun. In the game this mix of American hull and Soviet gun can engage from much farther away than the standard LVT(A)(4), and despite light armour it is a serious opponent for vehicles of similar rank. Its tall shape and open-topped turret leave it very exposed to strafing aircraft and artillery. It was a 2016 "Winter Holiday" event reward in Update 1.65, later sold as a Warbonds trophy in April 2019.
us_lvt_a1_m24: In 1944 the US military proposed fitting the LVT(A)(1) with an M24 turret and its 75 mm gun, but the widened turret ring made the vehicle unstable when firing afloat; a redesign was planned when Japan's surrender ended the programme, and the lessons fed into a 76 mm version. In the game it swaps the regular LVT(A)(1)'s 37 mm for a 75 mm whose APCBC rounds do far more damage after penetrating, and it gains a heavy machine gun. The cost is a larger silhouette, unchanged armour and a slower reload. It came with Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
us_lvt_a_1: Pacific landings showed the Marines needed more than heavy machine guns for fire support, so the LVT amphibian family gained the LVT(A)(1), with an M3-style turret carrying a 37 mm gun stabilised to shoot while afloat and extra machine guns on the rear deck; 509 were built. In the game it is an entry-level light tank with firepower close to the M3 light tank and the rare ability to cross water. The thin plating needed for buoyancy stops little beyond rifle-calibre fire, but it gives newcomers a distinctly different way to play. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
us_lvt_a_1_trb: An FMC amphibious tank derived from the LVT-2, the LVT(A)(1) carried a lightly modified M3 Stuart turret; 510 were built between December 1943 and late 1944 for US Army and Marine assaults on Japanese-held islands. This version, with its own camouflage, was given out in 2023 to players who used TheRussianBadger's partner link. In the game its gun reloads quickly and penetrates respectably, but armour is limited and the huge hull is hard to hide; even so, it adapts well to both aggressive and cautious play.
us_lvt_a_4: When Marines judged the LVT(A)(1)'s 37 mm too weak, the LVT(A)(4) took a modified turret from the M8 Scott howitzer carriage, adding a roof-mounted 12.7 mm Browning and dropping the rear-deck machine guns; 1,890 were built, most for the US Army and 50 for Britain. In the game this premium beginner light tank matches the M8's firepower while being able to swim, though its thin hull stops little beyond rifle-calibre fire. The slow shells can arc over low cover onto light vehicles, and the Browning handles light vehicles and slow, low aircraft well. It was a 2020 Victory Day reward in Update 1.97 "Viking Fury".
us_m10: Rushed out for the Tank Destroyer Branch formed after the fall of France, the M10 GMC put a high-velocity 3-inch gun in a large open-topped turret on an M4A2 Sherman hull and served from Tunisia to the end of the Second World War; the "Wolverine" name is probably post-war. In the game it shares the Sherman's drivetrain with a more sloped hull, and the 3-inch gun, which has no muzzle brake unlike later 76 mm weapons, penetrates most enemies it lines up on. Slow turret traverse is the big weakness, making it hard to react to surprise threats. It came with Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
us_m103: Alarmed by the IS-3's debut at the 1945 Berlin parade, the US began the T43 heavy tank in 1948 and rushed it into production during the Korean War, which led to lengthy rebuilds; 300 were standardised as the M103, mostly for the Marine Corps, and served until 1974. In the game everything centres on its huge 120 mm gun, whose HEAT rounds can deal with anything it meets. The armour is a bonus rather than a shield, since HEAT and APDS defeat the front fairly easily, though the rounded, uneven shapes cause some ricochets. It is slow and lags behind most allies. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m109a1: Entering US service in 1973, the M109A1 upgraded the M109 howitzer with the longer 155 mm M185 gun, stretching range from 14.6 km to 18 km; it backed US forces in Europe and the Middle East, and survivors were later converted to M109A2 standard. In the game it resembles the Soviet 2S3M, lobbing heavy 155 mm shells a long way with a poor rate of fire but plenty of ammunition. Good speed and acceleration let it relocate and avoid direct fights, which matters because its armour is thin, and low gun depression rules out shooting down from high ground. It arrived in "Kings of Battle".
us_m10_booker_late: Named after two decorated soldiers, the M10 Booker came from the US Army's Mobile Protected Firepower programme, launched in 2015 to give infantry brigades a direct-fire vehicle they had lacked since the Sheridan's retirement; General Dynamics' Griffin II, on the ASCOD 2 chassis, won in 2022, but the Army cancelled it in April 2025 after only 26 had been built. In the game it is a sensor-rich light tank whose thermal sights and an IRST able to follow low-flying aircraft make it a strong scout, backed by a 105 mm gun to exploit what it finds. It was added in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
us_m1128_mgs: The Mobile Gun System member of the Stryker family was developed by General Dynamics Land Systems for the US Army's Interim Armored Vehicle programme; 142 were built from 2002, but maintenance costs and weaker protection than other Strykers led to retirement by 2021. In the game it is a fast wheeled vehicle with a 105 mm gun and M900 ammunition, putting its firepower near the IPM1. Anything above autocannon calibre goes through its armour, even with the optional slat kit, so scoot-and-shoot is the way to play. Only 5 degrees of gun depression and a tall profile make safe firing spots harder to find. It arrived in "New Power".
us_m1128_wolfpack: Derived from Canada's LAV III Kodiak and in US Army service from 2006, the M1128 Stryker wheeled assault gun has steel hull armour backed by ceramic plates, rated against 14.5 mm fire, and can take slat screens against RPGs and missiles. Its name honours two posthumous Medal of Honor recipients, Stuart and Robert Stryker. The Wolfpack differs from the regular M1128 only in lacking hull slat screens and wearing a forest camouflage, so it keeps the same quick handling, light armour and capable armament. It was added in Update 2.23 "Apex Predators".
us_m1296_dragoon: The Dragoon came from a 2015 effort to up-gun the M1126 Stryker for the 2nd Cavalry Regiment in Germany, adding a remotely operated 30 mm turret to fill the gap between the machine-gun Stryker and the 105 mm MGS; 81 were converted, entering service from December 2017. In the game it shares the Stryker's excellent mobility, suiting both point capture and surprise flanks, and its fast-firing Bushmaster II has an APFSDS belt. It is large and lightly armoured, has only two crew and carries no ATGMs for heavier targets. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
us_m163_vulcan: Early in the Vietnam War the 40 mm Bofors of the M42 Duster could not fire fast enough against jets, so the US adapted the 20 mm Vulcan rotary cannon from its own aircraft as the M168 and mounted it with a tracking radar on an M113 chassis; Stinger-armed systems such as the Avenger eventually replaced it. In the game its huge rate of fire is the main asset, though range and overall capability fall short of the Gepard, Marksman or ZSU-23-4. That pushes it fairly close to the front, where it must take care not to be spotted by tanks. It was added in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
us_m18_hellcat: Buick's T70 was the fast, 76 mm-armed tank destroyer the US Tank Destroyer Branch had wanted since the fall of France; ordered into production as the M18 GMC in summer 1943 and nicknamed "Hellcat" by its builder, it fought at the Bulge among other battles. In the game it is extremely fast and agile, and its fully rotating turret gives a wider field of fire than casemate destroyers at the cost of a taller profile. Only 12.7 mm of armour means almost anything gets through, though AP shells sometimes pass straight out the other side. Added in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it was reclassed as a light tank in May 2021.
us_m18_hellcat_black_cat: A gift twin of the regular M18 Hellcat, the "Black Cat" differs very little in performance. Sold in a pack from Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it left the store after the sixth anniversary sale and returned for the seventh as a Golden Eagle purchase. APCR shells for its 76 mm gun give it an answer to common opponents such as the Panther D, Tiger H1 and IS-1. The fully rotating turret allows a wider arc of fire than casemate destroyers like the StuG III, at the price of a slightly taller shape, and high agility makes flanking its strength.
us_m18_hellcat_kit_3rank: This Hellcat represents the M18s that served with tank destroyer battalions of Patton's 4th Armored Division, fighting at Arracourt in September 1944 and at Noville near Bastogne, where four from the 705th helped paratroopers against the 2nd Panzer Division. Compared with the tech-tree M18 it adds extra armour, a camouflage net, an identification plate fitted so Allied troops would not mistake it for a German tank, and a 7.62 mm Browning. In play it is the familiar fast flanker with a strong 76 mm gun and APCBC shells, held back by thin armour and an open turret roof. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
us_m18_super_hellcat: To spread 90 mm firepower as widely as possible once the M36 arrived, US designers simply set an M36 turret on the nimble M18 hull; the result, called the "Super Hellcat", worked, but the war ended before it could be produced. In the game it pairs the M36's firepower with the M18's mobility, so the 90 mm defeats armour the 76 mm cannot. The M82 shell is the highlight: fired into flanks, which its speed helps it reach, its strong post-penetration damage can often knock out a tank with one hit. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
us_m19: Twin 40 mm Bofors on an M24 Chaffee chassis made the M19 MGMC, completed at the end of 1944 but not operational until after the war; its first combat came in Korea in 1950. The M19A1 adds a small auxiliary engine-generator so the guns work with the main engine off, plus stowage for two spare barrels. In the game it is versatile: AP and HE belts let the Bofors hurt light vehicles as well as aircraft, and its agility allows early flanking. Most of the crew sit in the open, though, with ammunition stored around the turret. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m1_abrams: After the MBT-70 and XM803 were cancelled, Chrysler's design beat General Motors for the XM1 contract in November 1976 and was accepted in 1981 as the M1 Abrams; 2,374 were built, and the type was upgraded repeatedly, eventually with a 120 mm gun. In the game it opens the American Abrams line, its turbine giving great speed and acceleration for repositioning and hit-and-run play. The armour is a clear step up, solid against kinetic rounds and especially strong against HEAT. It keeps the late M60's 105 mm gun and ammunition, but its mobility helps it reach enemy weak spots. It came with Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm".
us_m1_abrams_kvt: A premium gift tank from the "La Royale" update, the M1 KVT is an Abrams disguised with Soviet-style features. Unlike the real vehicle, which was converted from an M1A1, the in-game version is based on the original M1. Its disguise includes a rubber-fabric front screen in place of the side skirts, a netted barrel, a dummy IR searchlight, mock ERA blocks on the turret and glacis, two external fuel drums at the rear and turret boards reading "ЛОДКА" ("boat"), while the loader's M240 has been removed.
us_m1_ip_abrams: The Improved Performance M1 brought the stronger turret armour developed for the 120 mm M1E1 to the 105 mm Abrams, along with a turret bustle rack and trimmed rear skirts; 894 were built from 1984 to 1986, and it took part in the 1987 Canadian Army Trophy and Desert Shield without seeing combat. In the game the thicker composite in the turret cheeks resists both kinetic and HEAT rounds better than on the M1, encouraging more aggressive play, and the M900 APFSDS round penetrates more easily. The hull is unchanged, and the big turret ring remains vulnerable. It was added in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
us_m1a1_abrams: Fitted with the 120 mm M256 smoothbore after trials on the M1E1, the M1A1 was accepted in 1984 and built from 1985 to 1993; counting rebuilt M1s and IPM1s, around 5,000 exist, and it fought in Desert Storm and Iraqi Freedom. In the game it gives the fast Abrams the 120 mm gun, with only APFSDS and HEAT-FS available, and better-protected enemies may still need shots on weak points. Its composite armour holds well against HEAT and against kinetic rounds from weaker opponents, but mobility is the defence against stronger ones. Blow-out panels over the bustle ammunition help stop a cook-off from destroying it. It came with Update 1.87 "Locked On".
us_m1a1_abrams_yt_cup_2019: Awarded to the teams that won the 2019 YouTube Cup, this M1A1 arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy"; only its unique camouflage sets it apart from the standard tank. Historically, the M1A1 gave the Abrams the 120 mm M256 smoothbore, entering service in 1984 with around 5,000 eventually built or converted, and it saw combat in Desert Storm and Iraqi Freedom. In play it keeps everything the regular M1A1 offers: it survives hits well, moves superbly and carries potent ammunition, which puts it among the best main battle tanks in its bracket.
us_m1a1_aim_abrams: Australia bought 59 refurbished M1A1 AIM tanks from the US to replace a Centurion and Leopard fleet judged unable to protect crews against modern threats; the AIM ("Abrams Integrated Management") rebuild adds sensors and communications, and the tanks entered Australian service in 2007. In the game it keeps most of the M1A1's strengths with upgraded armour and fire control on top. Its KE-W APFSDS penetrates less than the M1A1's M829A1 but still threatens most opponents it will meet. It was added in "Danger Zone" as a squadron unlock.
us_m1a1_hc_abrams: Developed after the US Marine Corps chose the Abrams to replace its M60A1s, this M1A1 variant with Marine-requested changes went into production in November 1990 and served both services; the Army called it the M1A1 HC ("Heavy Common"), the Marines simply the "Common". In the game it adds the Heavy Armor upgrade with depleted uranium inserts and gains the M830A1 HEAT-FS round, whose proximity fuse lets it threaten low-flying aircraft too. Mobility is much as before, so it is essentially a stronger M1A1. It came with the "Direct Hit" update.
us_m1a1_hc_usmc: Click-Bait is a real Marine Corps M1A1 HC that became an internet curiosity after a photo showed it on deployment with a plastic garden chair on its roof; like other Marine HCs it carries the AN/VLQ-8A soft-kill protection system, a feature not found on other main-line Abrams. The premium version reproduces the chair and the kill markings on its barrel and otherwise matches the tech-tree M1A1 HC. Its mobility gets it to good positions quickly, and a quick reload lets it finish off targets that survive the first shot. It arrived in "Air Superiority".
us_m1a1_hc_usmc_sm: Developed for the US Marine Corps from 1992 on the basis of the M1A1 HA, the M1A1 HC gained second-generation depleted uranium armour, a soft-kill protection system and digital engine management; 880 were built, serving the Army and Marines in Iraq and Afghanistan. This version, from the 2025 Senrai Maidens event, wears a unique look based on the character Kate but otherwise matches the regular tank: mobile, with excellent turret protection, strong ammunition and electro-optical countermeasures against some ATGMs. Even early APFSDS gets through the hull, so keeping it behind cover matters.
us_m1a2_abrams: Production of the M1A2 began in 1992, and its headline feature was IVIS, which automatically shares battlefield information between units, alongside better armour and new fire control including an all-round commander's sight; about 2,200 were built or converted and serve with the US, Australia, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Morocco. In the game its depleted uranium turret package resists even advanced kinetic rounds, and the commander's thermal sight improves awareness. The added weight costs a little speed, and the hull stays weak even against modest APFSDS, so terrain should hide it. It suits both aggressive and defensive play and arrived in Update 1.93 "Black Shark".
us_m1a2_sep2_abrams: Once the Future Combat Systems programme was cancelled, the Army committed to the Abrams for the long term and developed SEP v2 with new sights, computers, electronics and an auxiliary power unit, plus a CROWS remote mount for the commander's heavy machine gun; it entered service in 2008 and equipped every armoured brigade by 2013. In the game it differs from the M1A2 SEP mainly in the raised CROWS Browning and optional ARAT II reactive armour, and at around 66 tons it is less mobile; firepower is unchanged. Its chief appeal is letting a player bring two SEP-class Abrams into one battle without spending a backup. It came with "Air Superiority".
us_m1a2_sep2_abrams_trophy: The US Army chose Rafael's Israeli Trophy-HV active protection system for Abrams tanks stationed in Europe, planning up to 261 conversions, enough for four armoured brigades; Leonardo DRS won the supply contract in 2018, and Trophy-equipped M1A2 SEPv2s took part in Defender Europe 2020 in Germany. In the game the Trophy, already seen on the Merkava Mk.4M, holds six interceptors and covers all directions against ATGMs from helicopters or ground launchers. Otherwise it is the familiar Abrams with good turret armour and the strong M829A3 round, though 69.5 tons blunts mobility. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
us_m1a2_sep3_abrams: The third System Enhancement Package Abrams, shown publicly in 2015 and redesignated M1A2C in 2018, added an ammunition data link for programmable rounds, improved IFLIR thermals, the CROWS weapon station and the multi-mode AMP round; the first went to the 1st Cavalry Division in 2020, and Poland and Australia ordered 250 and 75 respectively. In the game its stronger turret and hull armour cope better with APFSDS, allowing more aggressive play, and it gains the programmable-fuze M1147 HE shell plus a camouflage net modification. The extra armour pushes weight to 69.8 tons, hurting mobility. It came with Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
us_m1a2_sep_abrams: A late-1990s programme, the System Enhancement Package upgraded existing M1A2s with a second-generation commander's thermal imager, an eye-safe laser rangefinder and a digital map display, reportedly stretching maximum engagement range to 4,000 m; some also got thicker turret front and side armour. In the game the better thermals help find enemies at range and in bad weather, and the optional TUSK kit hangs ARAT reactive blocks along the sides, making it more comfortable than earlier Abrams in both aggressive and defensive play. The hull is still vulnerable even to older APFSDS, so it needs terrain in front of it. It arrived in "Fire and Ice".
us_m22_locust: Requested by the British War Office in 1941 because the Tetrarch was not built for airborne work, the M22 Locust was an American glider-portable light tank for British airborne forces and one of the smallest US tanks, with a three-man crew in which the commander also loaded; an order of around 1,900 was cut to 830. In the game its low profile suits scouting from hilly ground for teammates, and its firepower is acceptable beside other early American light tanks. With no gun stabiliser, though, accurate shooting on the move is hard. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m247: Ford Aerospace's M247 Sergeant York DIVAD, named after the First World War hero Alvin York, put a radar-directed turret with twin 40 mm Bofors on an M48 Patton chassis in the late 1970s; despite using off-the-shelf parts, technical problems and cost overruns ended it in 1985 after 50 were built. In the game it is a very strong anti-aircraft vehicle, as proximity-fused 40 mm shells tear apart aircraft within about 2 km, letting it protect teammates before bombs are released. It also carries semi-armour-piercing ammunition, but that only troubles lightly armoured targets. It was added in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
us_m24_chaffee: The Ordnance Department's T24 aimed to combine Stuart running gear with better armour and a 75 mm gun, replacing the outclassed 37 mm Stuart; standardised in 1943 as the M24 "Chaffee", about 4,731 were built in 1944-45, and it first fought at the Battle of the Bulge before serving on into Korea. In the game it is a big step up from the Stuarts: just as quick forwards and in reverse, with sloped frontal armour and a larger crew, and above all a 75 mm gun giving it medium-tank firepower. That mix suits surprise flanking and scouting for the team. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m24_chaffee_tl: The M24 (TL) was a 2015 Thunder League gift, earned by completing five tank challenges, and comes with every participating team's camouflage plus access to APCR; otherwise it is the standard M24 Chaffee. It plays as a mobile flanker rather than a static gun, managing roughly 38 km/h ahead and 25 km/h backwards, which suits peeking out from behind cover, firing and backing away. Its 75 mm M6 gun matches the Sherman's M3 apart from a slower reload, and its shells penetrate reliably with few ricochets.
us_m26_pershing: Work on a Sherman successor that began with the T20 ended in the T26E3, which brought a 90 mm gun, torsion bars and heavier, well-angled armour; standardised as the M26 Pershing, it reached the fighting only in early 1945 with little effect on the outcome, then served in Korea after being reclassed as a medium tank. In the game it is slower and heavier than the Shermans, with middling specifications overall: its armour beats the M4's, but high-velocity guns at its rank still defeat it, and the 90 mm, especially the M82 shell, does heavy damage yet struggles with many front plates. It rewards skilled players and came with Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m26_t99: Possibly inspired by the Sherman Calliope, this M26 Pershing carried T99 launcher pods on each side of the turret with 44 rockets in total; trialled at Aberdeen at the end of 1945, it then vanishes from the record and was probably a victim of post-war budget cuts. In the game it is the standard M26 plus those rockets, which offer a quick follow-up option while the 90 mm M3 gun reloads. This premium tank was added in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
us_m26e1_pershing: The M26 was judged outgunned by the Tiger II's long 88 mm, and the 90 mm T15 of the T26E4 had cartridges too big for easy loading, so the M26E1 prototype received the 90 mm T54, giving similar power with smaller rounds; post-war budget cuts ended the project. In the game it is a standard M26 apart from the very long L/73 gun, which brings firepower close to the Super Pershing and T32 with a faster reload. The barrel sticks well out from cover and is easy to knock out, while armour and mobility match the M26. It came with Update 1.47 "Big Guns" and left sale after the 9th Anniversary Sale.
us_m2_medium: Begun in 1936 from M2 light tank components and in service by 1938, the M2 medium reflected inter-war infantry doctrine: four hull machine gun sponsons were its main weapons, with the 37 mm kept for enemy tanks, and rear deflector plates even let gunners bounce fire down into trenches. It never fought, but it paved the way for the M3 and M4. In the game it is the first American medium tank; the 37 mm handles light tanks, and its size means one hit rarely finishes it. Armour is mediocre and the turret turns slowly, yet it works in attack and defence. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m2a2: The M2A2 grew out of the T1 and T2 light tank prototypes of the 1920s and 1930s; after 17 single-turret M2A1s, it was redesigned with twin turrets and 239 were built, making it the US Army's main tank of the inter-war years. In the game it shows the pre-war idea of machine guns as a light tank's offensive weapon, with the M2HB .50 cal on the left and an M1919A4 on the right, though each turret partly blocks the other's arc of fire. Heavier armour on enemy tanks soon left it obsolete. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
us_m2a4: Watching the Spanish Civil War convinced the US that machine-gun light tanks like the M2A2 were inadequate, so the M2A4 added thicker armour and a 37 mm anti-tank gun; approved in May 1940, 375 were built by April 1942, and it was the main American light tank at the war's outbreak, fighting with the Marines on Guadalcanal before the M3 Stuart took over. In the game it is a reserve tank and a preview of the Stuart line: quick and nimble with a capable 37 mm, but poorly protected at close range. It can fight head-on or slip round to hit weak spots unseen. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m2a4_1st_armor_div: Built between May 1940 and April 1942, the M2A4 fought with the Marines, but the Army used it only for training, including in the 1st Armored Division, which kept its M2A4s until switching to the M3 Stuart just before Operation Torch in November 1942. This premium version, available since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals", plays much like the reserve M2A4 while giving new players extra research points and Silver Lions. Brisk mobility and an adequate 37 mm let it pick off targets and take objectives to boost rewards.
us_m36: With the M10's 3-inch gun struggling against the frontal armour of newer German tanks, the Ordnance Department tried a 90 mm gun in an M10-based turret late in 1942; standardised as the M36 in June 1944, it reached combat in Europe that October, replacing the M10, and later served in Korea. In the game the bigger gun makes Panthers and Tigers far easier to deal with than in the M10, and small engine changes make it noticeably faster, so it reaches key positions quickly. Its armour is thin, and the open top leaves it exposed to strafing aircraft. It came with Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
us_m36b2: Starting in May 1945, 672 M10 hulls were converted to M36B2s by the American Locomotive Company, with 52 more from Montreal Locomotive Works; with Germany surrendering that month they missed the Second World War, but US and South Korean forces used them heavily in Korea, and with M26s and M46s scarce they became a favourite for military aid. In the game it behaves almost exactly like the M36, with added turret covers that stop light shrapnel and small-calibre strafing, though heavier aircraft guns still get through. New HEAT-FS ammunition lets it hit heavily armoured targets reliably at much longer range. It arrived in "Drone Age".
us_m3_bradley: The US search for an infantry fighting vehicle, begun in 1964, eventually settled on FMC's XM723, reworked into infantry and cavalry versions approved for production in 1980 as the M2 and M3 Bradley; the M3 trades passenger space for more ammunition for its 25 mm M242 chain gun and TOW missiles. In the game it is big and thinly armoured against both kinetic and HEAT rounds, with merely adequate mobility. Its weapons make up for that: autocannon APDS penetrates many tanks from the side and shreds light vehicles, while TOWs give a sure hit at range, though the launcher is slow to deploy after stopping. It arrived in Update 1.85 "Supersonic".
us_m3_lee: Germany's successes with the Panzer III and IV in France pushed the US to demand a 75 mm-armed medium tank quickly; the M3, begun in July 1940 and produced from late that year partly to meet a British order for 3,650 tanks, was always an interim design and left most fronts once Shermans were plentiful. In the game it outguns and outarmours the M2 medium, but its tall shape, hull-mounted 75 mm with a narrow firing arc, rivets and weak cross-country performance hold it back. It is an unusual tank that needs careful coordination to use well. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m3_stuart: Prompted by the fall of France and the obvious ageing of the M2, US designers produced the M3 light tank with thicker armour, revised suspension and a new recoil system; it was built from March 1941 to October 1943, and its chassis underpinned other vehicles such as the M8 Scott. In the game it shares much with the M2 family but has a stronger engine, slightly better armour and a more dependable transmission, making it very easy to move around. It plays as a light attacker or scout and is a good first tank for learning American ground forces. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m3a1_stuart: The second M3 light tank variant added a new turret with a basket and no cupola, an improved gun stabiliser and a taller anti-aircraft M1919A4 mount, while dropping the sponson machine guns; 4,621 were built, the last in February 1943. It first saw major action in Operation Torch in November 1942, doing well against early light tanks but suffering against up-gunned Panzer IIIs and IVs because of its flat, boxy hull. In the game it continues the M3 line and plays much like the other early American light tanks. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m3a1_stuart_usmc: The M3A1 Stuart brought a new turret with stabilisers, hydraulic traverse and a basket, and from 1942 it equipped the US Marine Corps through its Pacific campaigns; in 1944 the Marines turned 24 into flamethrower tanks nicknamed "Satan" for the Marianas battles. This version, included in the US Starter Pack, is the tech-tree M3A1 in a unique camouflage. It keeps a light tank's agility, and although the 37 mm feels weak at its level it can still exploit weak spots, so patience pays: wait for enemies to pass by or become distracted, then strike their flanks. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m3a3_bradley: After the A1 and A2 versions that fought in Desert Storm, the Bradley's late-1990s A3 upgrade focused on digitisation, adding networked communications, a Commander's Independent Thermal Viewer, new fire control and GPS; full-rate production began in 2001, the cavalry version becoming the M3A3. In the game a laser rangefinder and 25 mm APFSDS sharpen its gunnery, while TOW-2A roughly doubles the old missile's penetration and TOW-2B attacks from above. Extra plates improve the armour slightly, but most autocannons still get through, and the added weight slows it a little. It arrived in "Ixwa Strike".
us_m41_walker_bulldog: Seeking a more air-portable light tank with a high-velocity 76 mm gun, the US produced the M41, named "Walker Bulldog" to honour General Walton Walker, who lost his life in Korea; the M41A1 added hydraulic turret traverse and more ammunition stowage. It proved too heavy for air drops but served American and allied forces until the M551 replaced it. In the game its 76 mm M32 hits very hard, particularly with APDS, and good mobility and a low profile make it a natural scout and flanker. Top speed is modest, but strong acceleration lets it advance or retreat quickly. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m42_duster: Built by General Motors' tank division between 1952 and 1960 on the M41 chassis, the M42 "Duster" carries twin 40 mm M2A1 Bofors and stayed in service until 1988; in Vietnam it proved effective against unarmoured ground troops despite being designed for air defence. In the game it is fast and lightly armoured, so it should avoid anything its guns cannot penetrate and use its speed to reach enemy flanks early. Against aircraft a single direct hit can down even large planes. Most of the crew sits fully exposed, so cover and watching for strafing aircraft are essential. It arrived in Update 1.47 "Big Guns".
us_m44: An early-1950s successor to the M41 Gorilla, the M44 placed a 155 mm howitzer on a reversed M41 Walker Bulldog chassis; the first 250, built as enclosed T99E1s, filled with gun fumes, so all were recalled and rebuilt with an open fighting compartment and the M45 gun by 1954. It served the US Army until the M109 took over in 1963 and was widely supplied to allies. In the game it is compact and mobile with a powerful gun firing HE or smoke, but thin armour and an open top make it vulnerable, a 30-degree traverse often forces hull turns, and the long reload favours distance. It arrived in "Storm Warning".
us_m46_patton: Post-war budget cuts ruled out a new tank, so from 1946 the US modernised its M26 Pershings; the changes were extensive enough that the result, first prototyped in 1948, became the M46. It fought in Korea from 1950 and, once newer types such as the M47 arrived, left US service but went abroad as aid. In the game it fixes the M26's two main weaknesses, mobility and firepower, and its HEAT-FS shell lets it take on most opponents. The armour is unchanged, though, so it needs to shoot first. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m46_patton_73_armor_bat: Developed from the M26 with a Continental AV1790-3 engine, an Allison transmission and a new gun, the M46 Patton was named after General George S. Patton; 1,160 were built, and from August 1950 they outclassed the T-34-85s they met in Korea. In early 1951 the 73rd Tank Battalion painted its M46s with tiger faces, hoping to play on local superstitions about tigers to unsettle enemy troops. This version, in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals", carries that scheme but plays like the standard M46: mobile, well armoured for a medium tank, armed with HEAT and APCBC, with good gun depression for flanking or seizing key points.
us_m47_patton_II: When the Korean War created an urgent need for tanks, the US took the turret of the experimental T42 medium and fitted it to the M46 hull; refined into the M47 Patton II, it had a short US career once the M48 arrived but equipped many allied armies in Europe and elsewhere. In the game it feels much like the M46, sharing its engine and transmission, so mobility is unchanged. It adds a slightly stronger HEAT-FS round and a coaxial .50 cal, and a more steeply angled glacis improves survivability a little. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m48a1_patton_III: An American medium tank added in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows", the M48A1 resembles the later M60 at first glance but is easy to tell apart. Its rounded turret carries a 90 mm gun with a T-shaped cylindrical muzzle brake and a fume extractor just behind it, with a square mantlet under a dust cover, and its hull is a curved casting rather than the M60's flat welded plates.
us_m4_sherman: The M4 followed the cast-hull M4A1 into production a month later, using a welded hull, the Continental R975 radial engine and the M3 Lee's 75 mm gun; most of its early faults were fixed before production, helping the Sherman's name for reliability, and 6,748 were built between July 1942 and January 1944, plus 1,641 M4 (105) howitzer tanks. In the game it plays like the other early Shermans, with a 56-degree glacis and the better-protected M34A1 mantlet. Protruding driver hatches break the slope and draw fire, and the appliqué plates over the side ammunition show enemies where to aim. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4_sherman_calliope: The T34 Calliope was one of several US experiments mounting rocket launchers on the Sherman to swamp infantry attacks and dug-in positions faster than the 75 mm could, and it took its name from a steam organ, after its look and the roar of its rockets. In the game it carries 60 114 mm M8 HE rockets alongside its 75 mm M3 gun; volleys can wreck light vehicles, leave heavier ones with long repairs and even blind targets with smoke and fire, but several are usually needed per target and they are no substitute for the gun against tanks. Firing also gives its position away. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
us_m4_sherman_promo: The Sherman was Rock Island Arsenal's early-1940s answer to the M3 Lee's hull-mounted gun; the first prototype was ready in September 1941, and it entered service as the cast-hull M4A1 and welded-hull M4, later serving with many armies during and after the war. This camouflaged M4 was released in 2023 as a reward for tasks in War Thunder Mobile. In the game its quick-firing gun penetrates respectably and does good damage after penetration, and a vertical stabiliser helps it shoot on the move. Mobility is middling and the armour has many weak spots, but it works in attack or defence.
us_m4_t26: As Panthers and Tigers grew tougher and more common, and the 76 mm gun disappointed against them, the US tested a T26 Pershing turret on a Sherman hull in 1944; the conversion worked, but it would not have reached the front any sooner than the M26 itself, so it was dropped. In the game the 90 mm gun lets it tackle heavily armoured opponents, even heavy tanks, while handling like a familiar Sherman. The extra weight burdens the hull, Sherman armour no longer holds up, and the tall hull raises the turret, making it easy to expose the hull to high-velocity guns. It arrived in the "La Royale" update.
us_m4a1_1942_sherman: Named after Civil War general William T. Sherman and built in roughly 50,000 examples, a total beaten only by the T-34, the Sherman was the Allies' most common tank; the cast-hull M4A1 was its first major variant, introduced in February 1942, with 6,281 built by December 1943. In the game it is the first dependable American medium, with a 75 mm M3 gun in a fully rotating turret. Its rounded cast hull has weak spots at the flat-angled side joints and vision blocks, and the smaller M34 mantlet trades turret protection for 2 degrees more gun depression. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4a1_76w_sherman: The first late-generation Sherman combined the M4A1's cast hull with a reworked T23 turret mounting the 76 mm M1, a two-piece loader's hatch and water-protected "wet" ammunition racks. Shipped to England before D-Day, these tanks at first went unused because crews had not trained on them and nobody wanted another ammunition type to supply, though 76 mm Shermans later fought hard in Israeli service. In the game the 76 mm brings a clear gain in penetration and ballistics, but the armour is unchanged and most opponents penetrate it easily, so it relies on mobility to grab key positions rather than trading shots. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4a2_1944_germ: The M4 748 (a) represents an M4A2 taken over by the Wehrmacht and was the game's very first Sherman, offered as a pre-order during the ground forces closed beta and later in limited runs for the 5th anniversary, German Unity Day's 30th anniversary and the 10th anniversary, so new players generally cannot get it. It looks like a normal M4A2 apart from a dunkelgelb, rotbraun and olivgrün scheme similar to the Panther G's default. It plays like other Shermans: armour and gun are only adequate, but mobility lets it reach objectives and enemy flanks, or it can back up a stronger tank.
us_m4a2_76w_sherman: The second late-generation Sherman paired the M4A2's twin GM diesel with a T23-type turret and the 76 mm M1 gun; about 3,230 were delivered by May 1945, many to the Soviet Union, which favoured diesel tanks. In the game it has an unbroken welded glacis at 47 degrees and ammunition moved to the centre of the hull, but the front still fails against Panthers, Tiger Is and T-34s. Its very tall profile makes it easy to spot, so the best approach is to use its good early mobility to reach a hull-down spot and fire first. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4a2_sherman: The third early Sherman variant combined a welded hull with the GM 6046, two coupled diesel engines, and later examples got a one-piece 47-degree glacis; of 10,968 built across all turret types, most went to Britain, with others to the Soviet Union and the US Marines, while the US Army barely used it. In the game it is among the best early Shermans, as its uninterrupted welded glacis removes the M4 and M4A1's frontal weak points, although most opponents can penetrate it anyway. Without the cheek appliqué plate, the turret beside the mantlet is weak even to small guns. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4a3_105_sherman: In Italy, units up against strong fortifications were using the poorly suited M7 Priest for direct fire, which showed that a Sherman with a howitzer was worth having; production began in February 1944, and Chrysler built 4,680, including 2,539 M4A3 (105) HVSS, which served in Europe, the Pacific and Korea. In the game its 105 mm fires only HE and HEAT, but most opponents have thin spots those rounds exploit. The single-slope late hull gives up to about 100 mm of effective frontal armour, and the M4A3 engine and HVSS suspension make it smooth and mobile, though there is no stabiliser. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4a3e2_76w_sherman_jumbo: In February 1945 about 100 M4A3E2 assault tanks were re-armed in the field with the 76 mm M1, which their gun mount had been designed for; the hard part was replacing the ammunition racks, roughly 75 hours of work per tank, and the "Jumbo" nickname appears to be post-war. In the game the 76 mm finally gives the heavy Sherman the penetration to beat enemies from the front. Facing tougher opposition, though, its thick front no longer stops incoming fire reliably, so more caution is needed than in the 75 mm version. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4a3e2_sherman_jumbo: Needing a heavily armoured assault tank for Northwest Europe in 1944, with the T26E1 not ready, the US Army up-armoured the M4A3: extra plates took the hull front to 101 mm, a T23-based turret was about 152 mm thick, and a massively reinforced mantlet covered most of the turret face. Only 254 were built, and the "Jumbo" nickname is likely post-war. In the game most opponents at its level struggle to penetrate its front, so it can lead pushes and draw fire away from teammates. The 75 mm M3 lacks penetration against most enemies head-on, though, so flanking is often needed. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4a3e2_sherman_jumbo_cobra_king: Cobra King was the M4A3E2 of Company C, 37th Tank Battalion, 4th Armored Division, which in December 1944 became the first tank into besieged Bastogne to relieve the 101st Airborne; it had been knocked out in France the month before, repaired and returned, and was led that day by Lieutenant Charles Boggess under battalion commander Creighton Abrams. The premium version plays like the standard Jumbo: its front shrugs off most opponents' shots, so it can lead attacks and soak up fire, but its 75 mm struggles head-on, so it often disables guns and tracks first or works round to the sides. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4a3e8_76w_sherman: The M4A3 (76) W HVSS, popularly the "Easy Eight", paired the 47-degree glacis, wet stowage and a T23 turret with a muzzle-braked 76 mm M1 with new horizontal volute spring suspension that cured the older VVSS's problems; it fought late in the war in Europe and the Pacific, then in Korea, Vietnam and many foreign armies. In the game HVSS makes it the most mobile Sherman, though its tall profile is hard to hide, so using early speed to reach a hull-down spot and fire first works well. Track sections can be added for protection at some cost to mobility. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m4a3e8_76w_sherman_kit_3rank: The Detroit Arsenal-built "Easy Eight" reached Europe in December 1944 in time for the Ardennes, where Third Army's 4th Armored Division used it in the Battle of the Bulge, and around 540 had arrived by the war's end. The Sherman (Hell) represents field-modified tanks whose crews, worried by German hand-held HEAT weapons, added sandbags and concrete to the front; these did little against shaped charges but lifted morale. In the game it is a versatile backbone tank with decent mobility and a stabilised 76 mm, but its large size and poor armour leave it vulnerable to almost anything. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
us_m4a5_ram_2: Canada's Ram II cruiser used the chassis of the American M3 medium with a new turret carrying the British 6-pounder; the first prototype appeared in November 1941, but the Sherman outclassed it, so it was kept as a training tank in Britain up to mid-1944, with some hulls converted to other roles. The US labelled it M4A5 under its engine-and-hull naming system, though it is not a Sherman. In the game it mixes the M3 Lee's running gear and mobility with a turreted 6-pounder and plays like a standard American medium; beware the weak spot beside the hull machine gun mount. It came with Update 1.61 "Road to Glory".
us_m50_ontos: Named with the Greek word for "thing", the M50 Ontos carried six M40 recoilless rifles, officially called 106 mm; dropped by the Army in 1955, it went to the Marines, who received 297 and used them well in Vietnam, where volleys flattened fortifications and the light vehicle could slip away quickly. In the game its six HEAT or HESH rounds can be fired in rapid succession from a limited-traverse mount with 10 degrees of depression, making flank ambushes deadly even against thick armour. There is essentially no armour and the full reload is slow, so it plays like a fragile light tank. It arrived in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
us_m55: Developed from 1950 alongside the M53 on a modified M47 chassis, the M55 carried a 203 mm howitzer and was chosen for production after 1952 trials; it served mainly in Vietnam against fortifications until the M110 replaced it in 1969, and 550 were built, some for allies such as Belgium, West Germany, Spain and Taiwan. In the game its only real strength is the 203 mm HE shell with about 23 kg of TNT equivalent, enough to destroy any tank when well placed. With just 10 rounds and a very long reload, a miss leaves its big, thinly armoured hull at the enemy's mercy. It arrived in "Tusk Force".
us_m551: Named after Civil War general Philip Sheridan, the air-droppable M551 carried a troublesome 152 mm gun-launcher able to fire both shells and the MGM-51 Shillelagh missile; poor survivability and reliability showed in Vietnam, and it later played Soviet opposition forces at the National Training Center until 2003. In the game its stock low-velocity HE and HEAT rounds drop sharply, limiting range at first, but the Shillelagh reaches beyond 3 km and wrecks almost anything it penetrates. Its armour is weak, so cover is essential. It came with Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
us_m551_76: When the PT-76 appeared, the US abandoned the T92 in favour of the amphibious XM551, and while the Shillelagh missile was delayed the Army tested other armaments, including the M41's 76 mm gun, before rejecting them as too weak. In the game this Sheridan's two-plane stabiliser makes it effective at firing on the move, and with its high mobility it can play more aggressively than other 76 mm light tanks, though it lacks the T92's HEAT-FS. Thin armour leaves it very exposed to artillery and aircraft, so positioning matters. It was the main reward of Battle Pass Season XIV, "Airborne General", in "Air Superiority".
us_m56_scorpion: Seeking more anti-tank firepower for airborne troops after a drop, the US put a 90 mm M54 gun on a small, light tracked chassis, accepted in 1958 as the M56 "Scorpion"; Cadillac built 150, which fought in Vietnam. In the game it weighs less than almost any other tank destroyer, yet carries the usual 90 mm ammunition, including HEAT-FS with up to 320 mm of penetration. Its engine moves it briskly over rough ground and its low profile helps it lie in wait, but with the crew in the open and next to no armour, even machine-gun fire can put it out of action. It arrived in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
us_m5a1_stuart: Because radial engines were scarce in wartime, the M5 Stuart replaced the M3's powerplant with twin Cadillac V8s and automatic gearboxes, which made it quieter, cooler, roomier and easier to train on, and it gained a sloped glacis and raised rear deck; 8,884 M5s and M5A1s were built before the M24 took over in 1944. The M5A1 saw wide use late in the war, notably in Normandy, mainly for scouting and infantry support. In the game it plays much like the M3 Stuarts and other early American light tanks. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m5a1_stuart_canadian_5st_arm: A gift M5A1 Stuart in a special livery with premium bonuses, the Stuart VI (5th CAD) was sold as a pack and withdrawn after the 2017 Victory Day sale, so it can no longer be obtained. Its quick-reloading 37 mm is best used against flanks, as head-on fights are risky when any hit can be fatal to the thin armour. Against heavy tanks such as the KV-1, it needs M51B1 APCBC and a point-blank shot into the turret ring or the engine from behind.
us_m5a1_stuart_td: The M5 Stuart swapped scarce radial engines for widely available Cadillac V8s, and the improved M5A1, with a new turret, better radio and a turret basket, kept the 37 mm despite criticism and suffered engine reliability problems; 6,810 were built from November 1942 to June 1944. The M5A1 TD, a 2021 Twitch-viewing reward, wears the markings of C-34 "Carol" of the 3rd Armored Division, now displayed near Carentan. In the game it is nimble, and good stabilisation lets it shoot on the move out to medium distances, but its armour stops only autocannons, the crew space is tight, and the 37 mm often fails to penetrate.
us_m60: A late-1950s successor built from the M48 Patton, the M60 swapped the 90 mm for a 105 mm gun, strengthened weak areas of armour and was the first American tank since the war to run on diesel; more than 15,000 of all versions were built, and variants served American and allied forces until the M1 Abrams displaced them in the 1990s. In the game it is a well-rounded tank that can support teammates or lead pushes on objectives, combining good mobility, solid armour and a 105 mm gun able to defeat even the toughest opponents it meets. It arrived in Update 1.51 "Cold Steel".
us_m60_120s: General Dynamics Land Systems began the M60-2000 in 1999 as an upgrade for countries still running Patton-family tanks, placing an M1A1 turret with the 120 mm M256 on an M60 hull; renamed 120S, it was offered in Europe and the Middle East, but the single 2001 prototype found no buyers and was dismantled in 2003. In the game the Abrams turret brings a gun that defeats most foes and armour that stops most shots. The M60 hull offers little protection, though, and the unchanged engine hauling the heavier turret makes it slower than earlier M60s. It arrived in "Alpha Strike".
us_m60a1: After the T95 was cancelled, Chrysler fitted its T95E7 turret, with better armour and more room, to an improved M60 hull along with a new engine and fire control; adopted in 1961 as the M60A1, 7,840 were built by 1980. From 1972 an add-on hydraulic system gave the gun two-plane stabilisation, creating the M60A1 (AOS). In the game it pairs strong armour and good mobility with a stabilised 105 mm, but APFSDS defeats the armour, its size makes it easy to see, and autocannons can get through the sides. It came with Update 1.61 "Road to Glory".
us_m60a1_rise_mod: The late-1970s RISE programme made the M60A1's engine more reliable, and later additions of passive night vision, smoke launchers and, in the late 1980s, ERA produced the M60A1 RISE (P). Marine Corps tank battalions took it into Kuwait in Desert Storm, its last major action, where despite its age it destroyed many Iraqi vehicles, including T-72Ms, T-55s and Type 69s. The Predator is styled after Army vehicles from the 1991 Gulf War. In the game its 105 mm M68 has HEAT-FS, HESH and APFSDS, but the ERA does little against the APFSDS most enemies fire. It arrived in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
us_m60a1_rise_passive_era: Upgraded from the late 1970s for better engine reliability, the M60A1 RISE later gained passive night sights for the crew, smoke launchers and, by the late 1980s, explosive reactive armour against shaped charges, becoming the RISE (P), a type several countries still use. In the game it improves on the M60A1 (AOS) with the M735 APFSDS round, smoke grenades and above all ERA, which greatly improves protection from HEAT. That ERA does nothing against APFSDS, though, and most tanks it faces rely on such rounds. It arrived in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
us_m60a2: Keen on guided missiles as tank armament, the US Army converted M60A1s with a new turret carrying the 152 mm gun-launcher also used on the Sheridan, firing shells or the Shillelagh missile; problems with the system and its delicate ammunition, plus a poor reception from troops, ended it after 526 were built. In the game it can blast lighter targets with HE overpressure, penetrate steel with HEAT or strike from range with the Shillelagh. Unlike the small, nimble M551, though, it is tall and less mobile, and while sturdier, weak spots such as the cupola stop it from tanking frontal fire. It came with Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
us_m60a3_slep: The M60 AMBT (Affordable Main Battle Tank) was a 2011 Turkish upgrade package by StandartBio, combining a 1,200 hp diesel, modern fire control with independent sight stabilisation, a 120 mm smoothbore, side skirts, turret slat armour and a commander's 25 mm cannon; it was offered to M60 users in Africa and Southeast Asia without success. In the game its excellent thermal sight and one-shot-capable 120 mm suit a supporting role or flanking runs, and good mobility gets it to key spots quickly. Its armour only stops HEAT and autocannon rounds of 30 mm or less, so positions need care. It was a World War season 3 reward.
us_m60a3_tts: Work on improving the M60A1 began in 1972, and in 1979 it was standardised as the M60A3 with a laser rangefinder, solid-state ballistic computer, gun thermal sleeve and M240 coaxial, soon followed by the gunner's AN/VSG-2 thermal sight that created the TTS model; the Marines still used some in the 1991 Gulf War. In the game thermals and the rangefinder make long-range hits much easier, and an unlockable APFSDS keeps it competitive against newer tanks. Armour and mobility are little changed from earlier M60s, so it cannot absorb modern firepower and works best as a support tank. It arrived in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
us_m6a1: Begun as the 50-ton T1 when war broke out in Europe, the M6 mounted a 3-inch gun and a 37 mm side by side in one turret; the welded T1E3 became the M6A1, but by the time production was possible the Army preferred the cheaper, more reliable Sherman, and just 40 M6-family tanks were built, 12 of them M6A1s. In the game hull 12.7 mm machine guns deal with light vehicles such as SPAA, and a Wright G-200 radial, as used in the B-17, keeps it reasonably mobile for its size. Its bulk, middling armour and slow reverse suit a second-line role. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_m6a2e1: After M6 production stopped at 40 vehicles, the Ordnance Department proposed rebuilding them with a 105 mm T5E1 gun and thicker front armour to tackle European fortifications, but Eisenhower rejected the idea in 1944, and only two were converted, without the extra armour, to test parts for the T29. In the game it has both the 105 mm and the stronger glacis; the gun handles most enemies, but the hull is vulnerable, so hull-down play with the strong turret front and 10 degrees of depression works best. Some players instead drive in reverse, letting the huge engine absorb hits at the risk of immobilisation. It was the Battle Pass Season III reward in "Ixwa Strike".
us_m7: Begun in 1941 as a 13-ton light tank with a stabilised 37 mm gun, the T7 programme kept growing, gaining a British 57 mm and then the American 75 mm M3, until at 24 tons it was reclassified as the M7 medium tank. Compared directly with the M4A3, it was judged inferior, and the project was cancelled in January 1944 with only six M7E2s and seven M7s completed. In the game it has average mobility and a stabilised gun with mixed results: good damage after penetration but trouble against heavily armoured targets. Its own armour is fairly weak. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
us_m728: The M728 Combat Engineer Vehicle traces back to the 1944 T39 demolition tank and the 1960 T118 testbed; built on the M60 hull and accepted in 1965, 328 were made, serving in Vietnam, the Gulf War and briefly with the FBI at Waco in 1993 before final retirement in 2018. In the game it resembles the British Centurion AVRE and shares its 165 mm demolition gun. M60 armour gives decent protection against late-war and Korean War-era vehicles, but chemical rounds are a problem. The very slow shell suits urban maps better than big, open ones. It arrived in Update 2.23 "Apex Predators".
us_m8_greyhound: Conceived in 1941 as a tank destroyer candidate, the T22 proved better suited to reconnaissance and was accepted in 1942 as the Light Armored Car M8, nicknamed "Greyhound" by the British; over 8,000 were built from 1943 to 1945, serving in several Second World War theatres and in Korea. In the game it ranks among the stronger early armoured cars, with a competitive 37 mm gun and a roof-mounted .50 cal that threatens low aircraft and thin-skinned light tanks. Its armour occasionally stops autocannon fire or deflects a shell, and it is fast on roads but weaker cross-country. It arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France" for the 5th anniversary.
us_m8_scott: Early trials putting a 75 mm M2 howitzer on the M3 light tank chassis produced a nose-heavy, cramped vehicle, so the gun moved to the new M5 chassis, whose sloped front gave more room and protection, and then into a manually rotated open turret, creating the 75 mm Howitzer Motor Carriage M8. In the game it plays like the LVT(A)(4) but is smaller and more mobile. The low-velocity howitzer is poor at long range, yet its arcing shells can be lobbed over low cover onto hidden enemies, giving it a distinct style among early American light vehicles. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
us_m8a1: In 1943 a test fitted the Sherman's 75 mm gun into the M8 howitzer carriage; it worked, despite little ammunition space and a cramped crew, and the Tank Destroyer Branch briefly saw it as a stopgap before the M18 Hellcat, but it would have arrived no earlier than the M18, so the project ended in June 1943. In the game it puts medium-tank firepower, much like the M24 Chaffee's, in a Stuart-sized package, suiting flanking and tank hunting despite poor armour and crew survivability. The open top invites strafing, though a roof .50 cal can fight back. It was a Winter 2014 gift and later a 4th-anniversary Warbond reward.
us_m901_itv: Built on the plentiful M113, the Emerson-designed Improved TOW Vehicle was adopted as the M901 in 1979 to give the Army a mobile ATGM platform; more than 3,000 were made, many exported, and in Desert Storm it scored 14 credited kills before US retirement began in the mid-1990s. In the game its raised "hammerhead" launcher lets it hide the whole hull behind cover and fire with only the small turret exposed. The launcher folds down while moving and must be redeployed, and the vehicle has to stay still to fire, so it suits patient positional play rather than aggression. It arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
us_magach_3: Israel's Magach 3 blends M48 and M60 features: the rounded cast M48 hull and turret carry a 105 mm M68 gun, while the engine and rear deck come from the M60. Distinctive touches include 20 smoke launchers beside the mantlet, a low-profile Urdan cupola that drops the commander's 12.7 mm for a pintle-mounted 7.62 mm Browning, and Blazer ERA in long vertical blocks over the hull front and the turret's front and sides, unlike the bolted tiles of the M60A1 RISE (P). This premium arrived as a pack in Update 1.77 "Advancing Storm" and was withdrawn when Israel's ground tree entered testing.
us_mbt_70: The MBT-70 was a 1960s US-West German project for a tank to counter new Soviet designs, featuring hydropneumatic suspension, spaced armour, a remote 20 mm mount, NBC protection and a 152 mm gun-launcher firing shells or Shillelagh missiles. Clashing doctrines and soaring costs led West Germany to leave in 1969, and the cheaper American-only XM803 was cancelled in 1971; the work fed into the M1 Abrams and Leopard 2. In the game its ability to launch missiles through its barrel, unusual for a Western tank, adds to a good balance of protection, speed and firepower that copes with most threats. It arrived in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
us_merkava_mk_1: After Britain declined to sell Israel the Chieftain, Israel Tal championed a home-grown tank informed by the 1973 Yom Kippur War; the resulting Merkava Mk.1 entered service in 1979 with a front-mounted 908 hp diesel, a licence-built copy of the 105 mm M68 and Centurion-derived running gear, and 180 fought in the 1982 Lebanon War, some converted into improvised carriers or ambulances. In the game the front engine, placed to protect crews that a small country could not afford to lose, gives it far better survivability than conventional main battle tanks. It was the 2019 "Battlefield Engineer" crafting event reward in Update 1.87 "Locked On".
us_merkava_mk_2b_late: Lessons from the 1982 Lebanon War produced the Merkava Mk.2, with more protection against shaped charges, new fire control, a new transmission and laser warning receivers; the Mk.2B added a thermal sight and extra turret armour screens. 580 Mk.2s were built from 1983 to 1989, none exported, and the last passed to the reserves in 2016. In the game composite screens on the hull and turret sides improve protection against HEAT and ATGMs compared with the Mk.1. The front engine shields the crew but is easily knocked out or set alight, and mobility is low by Western standards. It was a 2019 "Operation F.R.O.S.T." event reward.
us_merkava_mk_3d: The Merkava Mk.3D, or Dor-Dalet ("fourth generation"), was the final Mk.3 sub-variant, entering IDF service in 2000 with sloped modular composite armour on the turret sides similar to the Mk.4's, which also works as spaced armour, plus stronger CAT-supplied tracks. In the game the new modules bring turret protection close to the Mk.4 and help it survive ATGMs. Widely spaced crew and no ammunition in the turret make it very hard to knock out with one shot, especially when hull-down. It was a reward in the 2020 "Strategist" wargame event, added with "Raining Fire".
us_mim_72_chaparral: A cheap way to give the M113 short- and medium-range air cover, the Chaparral launched adapted AIM-9 Sidewinders and served the US from 1969 to the early 2000s; several countries bought it, and its sole confirmed success came when Israeli crews brought down a MiG-17 above the Golan. In the game its infrared missiles need no radar, so pilots get no lock warning, but flares and evasive flying can beat them. Ground-attack jets such as the A-10 and Su-25, which carry countermeasures and outrange it, are the main threat, and with no gun it cannot deal with targets too close for a lock. It arrived in "Sons of Attila".
us_mk1_grant: Short of equipment after France, Britain bought the M3 medium but had Rock Island Arsenal design a larger turret with room for a radio and no machine gun cupola; named after Ulysses S. Grant to tell it apart from the standard Lee, it served with British and Commonwealth forces. In the game the thicker turret front and missing cupola make it tougher than the M3 Lee, and its two guns, a quick 37 mm and a hard-hitting, stabilised hull 75 mm, can be bound to separate keys. Poor turret depression and a tall shape make very close targets awkward. It came as a bundle with Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
us_nasams_fcs: NASAMS was developed by Norway's Kongsberg with Raytheon from the 1980s to replace Improved Hawk, using ground-launched AIM-120 AMRAAMs guided by an AN/MPQ-64 Sentinel radar; it entered Norwegian service in the mid-1990s, and the NASAMS 3 version, with a new launcher able to fire AIM-9X and AMRAAM-ER, reached the US in 2019. In the game the system has three parts, and this TADS vehicle carries the Sentinel radar, which detects targets out to 20 km. It is unarmed and barely protected against shrapnel, and losing it disables the whole system, so careful concealment is vital. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
us_nasams_launcher: Developed by Kongsberg and Raytheon to replace Norway's Improved Hawk, NASAMS fires AMRAAM air-to-air missiles from ground launchers; the NASAMS 3 version entered US service in 2019 with a Mk.2 launcher for AIM-9X and AMRAAM-ER. In the game this TEL is one of two launchers controlled from the TADS vehicle and needs no separate research. It carries AIM-120C-7 or longer-ranged, thrust-vectoring AMRAAM-ER missiles, plus agile infrared AIM-9X Block IIs for closer targets. It is large, thinly protected, helpless against ground vehicles and useless if the TADS is destroyed. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
us_rdf_lt: AAI Corporation developed the RDF/LT after the HSTV-L trials of 1980, keeping the 75 mm XM274 but making the vehicle lighter for air transport, with simpler suspension, a 60-round autoloader and a diesel in place of the turbine; the services withdrew in 1982, ending the project. In the game it is largely a weaker HSTV-L: it keeps the compact size and 75 mm with more ammunition, but rifle-calibre machine guns can penetrate its armour, mobility is noticeably worse and the gun still lacks damage. It arrived in Update 2.43 "Storm Warning".
us_skink_aa: Canada built three prototypes of the Skink, a Sherman-based anti-aircraft tank, in 1943-44; the one sent to the 2nd Canadian Armoured Brigade in early 1945 never fired at aircraft but proved a potent weapon against infantry, and on one occasion a brief burst made a 45-man German company give up, and was later scrapped in Canada. In the game its fully enclosed M4A1-based hull and turret make it immune to aircraft cannon fire and bomb or rocket fragments, a rare advantage among SPAA. Four 20 mm Polsten cannons handle aircraft and light vehicles alike, but each barrel holds only 30 rounds. It arrived in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
us_skink_aa_kit_3rank: The Skink was a Canadian Sherman-based anti-aircraft tank of 1943-44; the one prototype that saw action, in early 1945, used its four 20 mm guns against infantry rather than aircraft. This version wears field modifications such as extra road wheels, track links and wooden panels, which gave little real protection but stopped magnetic mines and charges being attached, a particular problem in the Pacific. In the game its enclosed hull and turret shrug off aircraft cannon and fragments, but each barrel holds only 30 rounds and the guns cannot penetrate heavy tanks. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
us_sl_amraam_fcs: When the MIM-72 Chaparral aged out in the 1990s, Raytheon paired the HMMWV with ground-launched AIM-120 AMRAAMs, creating SLAMRAAM for the Army and CLAWS for the Marine Corps, with an AN/MPQ-64 Sentinel radar on a separate vehicle; first fired in 1997, CLAWS was cancelled in 2006, though Norway later adopted a derivative for NASAMS 3. In the game this TADS tows its radar on a trailer, so the truck can hide behind a building with only the trailer showing, and the radar scans quickly with fine resolution. With no armour and two crew, even small arms are dangerous, so its speed for repositioning matters. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
us_sl_amraam_launcher: CLAWS was the Marine Corps' HMMWV-mounted, Raytheon-built AMRAAM system meant to succeed the Chaparral; during development from 2001 its launcher grew from four to six rails and gained the option of two AIM-9X missiles, but budget cuts cancelled it in 2006. In the game this TEL is one of two launchers deployed from the TADS without extra research. Mixing radar-guided and infrared missiles lets the system cover the sky out to 15 km with no blind zone near the vehicle. Speed helps it relocate, but with no armour and only two crew, even small machine guns are a serious threat. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
