us_stingray: Cadillac Gage developed the Stingray as a private export venture in 1983; only Thailand bought it, taking 106, and its entry in the Armored Gun System contest to replace the M551 ended when that programme was cancelled in 1997. In the game it is a classic light tank, quick and agile, with a 105 mm gun firing strong APFSDS, plus a laser rangefinder and two-plane stabilisation for accurate long shots. The angled front can stop autocannon fire but should not be trusted, and the weak reverse speed makes escaping trouble difficult. It arrived in "Tusk Force".
us_t114: During development of what became the M113, the T114 was tried as a battalion anti-tank vehicle with a 106 mm M40A1 recoilless rifle in a turret with a semi-automatic loader feeding three ready rounds; two prototypes were tested in 1960-61 before the role was dropped and the design became the M114 command and reconnaissance vehicle. In the game its round, gun-topped turret looks like science fiction, and it is small, just over 2 m tall, nimble and well armed. Its HEAT rounds penetrate well and can be fired in quick succession at several targets, but the armour fails even against heavy machine guns. It arrived in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
us_t14: The T14 assault tank was a US-British project for a common infantry tank; by the time the prototype reached Britain in 1944 the Churchill was well established and much improved, so it went no further, and only two were built, one of which is now at Bovington. Britain's A33 "Excelsior" was built to the same requirement. In the game it is meant for breaking through defences: the 75 mm M3 reloads quickly, the armour soaks many hits, and a basic stabiliser helps firing on the move. A 61-degree glacis and upper sides as thick as the front make angling easy. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
us_t18_e2: Built to British requirements for a heavy armoured car, Yellow Coach's 8x8 T18 of 1942 first carried a 37 mm gun, then the 57 mm of the T18E2; weight, poor mobility and cost limited production, and the few built went to Britain for limited use in North Africa. It was the reward for six ground Chronicle awards in the 2018 "Chronicles of World War II" event during Update 1.77. Its armour keeps out 37 mm and can even stop 50 mm hits, and the accurate, quick-firing, stabilised 57 mm M1 with HE makes the "Boarhound" deadly. It is fast on roads but bogs down badly in mud or water.
us_t1e1: The 50-ton T1 heavy tank programme of 1940 paired a 3-inch gun with a 37 mm in one turret; the T1E1 version used a gas-electric drive, and its first prototype in May 1942 performed well enough to be considered as the M6A2, but a shift towards medium tanks capped M6 orders at 40, 20 of them T1E1s. In the game it moves noticeably better than the M6A1, letting the twin-gun turret keep up with medium tanks and reach better positions. Its huge size remains a liability, and enemies who reach its flank can knock it out quickly. It arrived in "Sky Guardians".
us_t1e1_90: As US doctrine shifted to mass-produced medium tanks in 1943, M6 development stalled, but trials at Aberdeen continued, including a T1E1 re-armed with the 90 mm T7 gun; the electrically driven chassis carried it well, though the turret was cramped and the design outdated, so it went no further. In the game the 90 mm penetrates very well and has a range of ammunition, including a strong APCBC shell, letting it tackle Tigers, Panthers and IS tanks at long range. Protection and mobility match the T1E1, but its towering silhouette is hard to hide on some maps. It arrived in Update 2.39 "Dance of Dragons".
us_t20: Intended to replace the Sherman, the T20 family led to a July 1943 proposal to standardise the 76 mm-armed T23E3 and T20E3 as the M27 and M27B1, but the Army saw no need to disrupt existing production and refused; the line eventually produced the M26 Pershing. In the game it is an offensive, mobile tank best used around cover and alongside teammates, since its armour is fragile. Think of it as a bulkier M18 Hellcat, flanking early and pulling back when things turn bad, helped by a very fast reverse, and changing position regularly keeps enemies guessing. It arrived in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
us_t25: The T25 was the 90 mm-armed version of the T23 medium; two converted prototypes arrived for testing in January 1944, but the complex electric transmission made it too heavy, and by summer 1944 combat experience favoured the better-armoured T26E1, which led to the M26. In the game it is essentially a smaller M26 with the same gun and engine, so mobility is similar but the thinner armour stops less. The 90 mm struggles with the heaviest tanks it meets, but fired into a flank, the M82 APCBC shell usually destroys whatever it penetrates. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
us_t26e4_superpershing: Facing the Tiger II's long 88 mm, the US developed the high-velocity 90 mm T15 and fitted it to a T26E1 prototype, known informally as the T26E1-1, which went to Europe in March 1945; the 3rd Armored Division added extra plates to the turret and hull and used it in combat until the war ended, after which it was scrapped. In the game it is an M26 with more armour and much more firepower; the extra weight slows it, but the 90 mm T15E1 can defeat the toughest tanks it meets. The long reload makes close-range brawling risky. It arrived in Update 1.57 "Battle March".
us_t26e5: Encouraged by the M4A3E2 Jumbo, the US began converting M26 prototypes with much heavier hull and turret armour in January 1945; the resulting T26E5 strained its suspension but performed acceptably, and only 27 were built before the war ended. In the game it is an assault tank for close-range fighting at the front: the excellent frontal armour stops many AP rounds, and the M26's 90 mm often kills with a single explosive-filled shell. Penetration can fall short against some opponents, though, and it is too slow to reach key positions ahead of others. It arrived in "Ground Breaking".
us_t28: Begun in 1943 to break fortifications such as the Siegfried Line, the T28 (at times designated T95) carried a 105 mm T5E1 gun behind 305 mm of frontal armour, crawled at 13 km/h and used removable outer tracks to spread its weight; when two prototypes reached testing in 1945 the Line had already fallen, and the project was cancelled in 1947. In the game "T28" is the transport version without the extra tracks, so ground pressure is high and mobility terrible, the sides are weaker and aircraft are a constant danger, though the gun and thick front remain. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
us_t29: The T29 heavy tank put a 105 mm T5 gun in a rotating turret instead of a fixed casemate like the T95's, with a strong mantlet over an angled yet rather thin hull; it arrived as a gift vehicle in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows", offered in advance as a pre-order bundle. In the game it is among the strongest heavy tanks of its era, alongside the Tiger II, IS-3 and IS-6. The T13 APCBC round often destroys a tank in one hit, the front absorbs most fire, and the high-velocity gun suits sniping too. Top speed is lower than its main rivals', but good acceleration helps in towns.
us_t30: Designed alongside the T29 and sharing its hull and turret with the T29 and T34, the T30 was an American wartime heavy tank project armed with a 155 mm gun, intended to deal with new German heavies like the Tiger II and Jagdtiger as well as Soviet IS tanks. In the game it is a premium gift that came with Update 1.85 "Supersonic", earned by collecting 10 tank Christmas Toys in the 2018-19 "Festive Quest" and afterwards sold on the Gaijin Market.
us_t32: The T32 can be thought of as a much-strengthened M26 Pershing, carrying a high-velocity 90 mm T15E2 gun and a turret front 298 mm thick; it has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals". Hull-down, the turret deflects most AP shells at any range, but HEAT-FS aimed at the gap below the mantlet, shots bouncing off the lower mantlet into the hull roof and ammunition, and very large HE shells are real dangers, as are the lower plate edges. The stock T43 AP lacks filler, so researching the T41 APCBC, with a 140 g charge, is a priority; T44 APCR penetrates further, and HE suits soft targets.
us_t32e1: Testing of the T32 showed its cast upper hull front was too weak, so prototypes three and four received a front made of two rolled plates and lost the hull machine gun, becoming the T32E1; completed in mid-1946, too late for the war, it never entered production, though ideas such as its cross-drive transmission later appeared in the M60 family. In the game it plays much like the T32, its strong armour and capable gun suiting the attack or defence of key points with teammates. Mobility is mediocre and the gun reloads slowly, so it is vulnerable when left alone. It arrived in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea".
us_t34: Developed in 1945 between the 105 mm T29 and 155 mm T30, the T34 carried a 120 mm T53 gun derived from an anti-aircraft weapon; two were converted from T30s in 1948, but violent recoil, turret fumes that hospitalised loaders and the family's weight led to cancellation in 1950, with the lighter M103 preferred. In the game its big armoured turret holds a 120 mm that penetrates any tank it meets, and six well-spaced crew make one-shot kills unlikely. Weak spots at the mantlet, machine gun port, roof and cheek ammunition, plus a long reload, make medium to long range its best setting. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
us_t54e1: Using an M48 hull, the T54E1 (105 mm Gun Tank T54E1) resembles the M48 and M103 at a glance but carries an oscillating turret of the kind used on French designs like the AMX-50. Its defining feature is a drum autoloader, again in the French style of the AMX-50 and Lorraine 40t, which sets it apart from other American tanks of its rank. In the game this premium pairs M48 hull armour with a strong 105 mm and that autoloader. It arrived in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
us_t54e2: The T54 programme, begun in 1951 after an Army recommendation for a new 105 mm tank gun, tried several ways of mounting the T140 on an M48 chassis; the T54E2 was the final version, with a conventional turret and no autoloader, and the project was dropped in 1957 in favour of the T95. In the game it plays like the M60, with decent armour, middling mobility and a strong 105 mm that suits support in attack or defence. It reloads far more slowly than L7-armed tanks, so close-range fights are best avoided. It arrived in Update 2.31 "Kings of Battle".
us_t55e1: Developed from the 8x8 "Cook Interceptor", the 3-inch Gun Motor Carriage T55 was built in November 1942 and refined into the T55E1 in April 1943; it performed reasonably on wheels but could not match a tank's mobility and agility, so it was rejected and sent to Aberdeen. In the game its wheels limit cross-country work and turning, but it is unusually fast forwards and in reverse for a 3-inch gun carrier. The gun sits far forward, so with good depression it can fire while exposing very little, suiting hit-and-run play. It was the reward for Battle Pass Season II, "Steel Centurion", in "Hot Tracks".
us_t58: Shortly after the M103 was fielded, the US began the T57 and T58, turreted heavy tanks on an improved, heavily armoured M103 hull with 120 mm and 155 mm guns respectively; the T58's modernised T30-type gun had a six-round drum autoloader, fume extractor and vertical breech. Approved in 1952, both were slowed by long production times and shifting requirements, then cancelled in 1957 and scrapped. In the game its 155 mm and quick autoloader can wipe out several enemies in seconds, but refilling the drum takes a long time. The tank is big, and three of four crew sit in the turret, often knocked out together. It arrived in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
us_t77e1: Work on a multi-gun anti-aircraft vehicle on the M24 chassis (then the T24) began in July 1943 with four machine guns, and officials asked for two more after seeing the mock-up; a T77 was completed in July 1945, followed by a second prototype, the T77E1, but the war was over and both were probably scrapped. In the game it is light and agile, and its six .50 cal Brownings shred aircraft with good aim. They can hurt some ground targets, but trading fire with tanks is unwise given its thin, if angled, armour. It arrived in "Firebirds".
us_t86: Inspired by Pacific experience, the 1944 Ritchie Project produced amphibious versions of the M18 Hellcat with a lighter, buoyant hull and M24-type tracks; Marmon-Herrington built three prototypes, and tests favoured the track-propelled T86, which managed 4-6 mph afloat while keeping M18-like performance on land. In the game it gives up the Hellcat's speed and some armour for the ability to swim, and its silhouette is huge. It still moves well on land and its excellent 76 mm suits flanking, but a water speed of 6 km/h and poor armour make open ground and open water dangerous. It was a reward in the 2025 Normandy '44 event in "Hornet's Sting".
us_t92: AAI's design to succeed the M41 Walker Bulldog was approved in 1954 as the 76 mm Gun Tank T92 and won its competition by 1956, but when Congress asked whether it could swim, after the Soviets fielded an amphibious light tank, and the answer was no, it was cancelled in favour of an amphibious design. In the game it presents a far smaller target than the M41A1 and shares its gun calibre, adding the M496 HEAT-FS round as a useful all-round shell alongside the stronger APDS. Its armour is thin, but crew and ammunition sit towards the rear, so frontal hits often strike other components first. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
us_t95: The T95 is the full, double-tracked form of the super-heavy assault vehicle begun in 1943 as the T28 to breach the Siegfried Line, with a 105 mm T5E1 gun behind 305 mm of frontal armour; called a gun motor carriage from 1945 because it had no turret, it was cancelled in 1947 after the Line had long fallen. In the game it is extremely slow but superbly armoured and armed, and it turns its hull towards threats surprisingly quickly. It can hold choke points almost alone and kills most targets it penetrates in one shot, but it draws aircraft and needs support. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
us_t95e1: The T95 medium tank programme aimed to replace the M48; the T95E1 dropped the base model's two-plane stabiliser and OPTAC fire control for a simpler system, and the programme was eventually cancelled over an inaccurate smoothbore, a troublesome transmission and little real gain over the M48, though its T95E7 turret led to the M60's "needle nose". In the game its 90 mm smoothbore makes it the first American tank with APFSDS. It lacks a stabiliser, rangefinder or thermals, but a reliable transmission, flat-shooting shells and a steeply sloped turret that deflects shots at range make it well rounded. It arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica".
us_xm1_chrysler: After the MBT-70 and XM803 were cancelled in 1971, the XM1 programme sought an affordable tank whose armour could stop the Soviet 115 mm gun at 800 m; Chrysler and General Motors delivered prototypes in 1976, and Chrysler's gamble on the AGT-1500 gas turbine won it the contract. The tank entered service in 1980 as the M1 Abrams. In the game its armour is light, but speed and agility suit flanking and seizing objectives, aided by thermals and a laser rangefinder. A roomy interior and ready ammunition behind blow-out panels in the turret bustle improve survivability. It arrived in Update 1.79 "Project X", once as an Xbox exclusive.
us_xm1_gm: General Motors' XM1 prototype, a premium gift added in Update 1.79 "Project X", looks like an M1 Abrams but should be played more like a Leopard or Ru 251, using speed, agility and its gun to hit weak spots rather than relying on armour. It has hydropneumatic suspension, an angled hull reminiscent of the Leopards, a combined gunner and commander sight, night sights for driver and commander and a thermal sight for the gunner. Its tracks are unusually loud, sometimes drowning out the engine, and its default paint is olive drab, switching to sand on desert maps.
us_xm246: General Dynamics began the XM246 in 1973 for the GLAADS programme and later reworked it for the 1977 DIVAD contest with twin Oerlikon KDA 35 mm cannons, Delco electro-optics and a fire-control radar adapted from the Navy's AN/VPS-2; Ford's XM247 won, the Army disliking the XM246's offset optics and radar, which struggled with fast crossing targets. In the game its rapid-firing 35 mm guns, as on the Gepard, work against air and ground targets, and the M48-based hull shields the crew from fragments. The big turret with side ammunition stowage is vulnerable, and it lacks the M247's proximity rounds. It arrived in Update 2.45 "Hornet's Sting".
us_xm_8: The Army's Armored Gun System programme, launched in 1981 to address the Sheridan's flaws, prompted FMC's CCVL, with an autoloaded 105 mm M68A1, optional add-on armour and many M113 and Bradley parts; six XM8 AGS prototypes were ordered in 1992, but the programme was cancelled in 1996, and a later bid lost the Mobile Protected Firepower contest to the M10 Booker. In the game a five-second autoloader, laser rangefinder and gunner's thermals make its 105 mm very effective, and it is fast. Armour only stops heavy machine guns and most crew sit in the turret; add-on kits help at the cost of weight and smoke launchers. It was a 2021 "Future Technology" event reward.
us_xm_800t: With the M114 scout proving unreliable in Vietnam, the US launched the XM800 Armored Reconnaissance Scout Vehicle programme in the 1970s; Lockheed's wheeled XM800W and FMC's tracked XM800T reached comparative trials in 1974, the tracked design edging ahead on off-road ability, but budget cuts and the priority given to what became the M2 Bradley ended it in 1975. In the game it is faster than almost anything near its rating, though it can roll over at speed. A quiet engine aids ambushes, and the quick-firing 20 mm handles light and medium targets and can engage aircraft, but ammunition is limited and the thin armour invites air attack. It arrived in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
us_xm_803: After West Germany left the MBT-70 programme, the US tried to make a cheaper all-American version, the XM803, using steel armour and a US engine; it ended up slightly heavier and slower, and as it grew as complex as the MBT-70, Congress cancelled it in December 1971, clearing the way for the XM1 and the M1 Abrams. In the game it plays almost exactly like the MBT-70, including firing ATGMs through the gun, a rarity among Western tanks, and keeps a good balance of protection, speed and firepower. It is a little slower and lacks the original's roof-mounted 20 mm cannon. It arrived in Update 1.79 "Project X".
us_xm_975_roland: The XM975 put the Franco-German Roland missile system, essentially Roland 2 with an American long-range search radar, on a modified M109 chassis after the US Army chose Roland in 1975; it first fired in 1978, but technology-transfer problems and rising costs killed the programme, leaving only 27 truck-mounted launchers for the National Guard. In the game it controls the airspace out to about 8.5 km, and its infrared search and track mode gives pilots no radar warning of a lock. With only 10 missiles on board, shots should not be wasted. It arrived in "Winged Lions".
ussr_2s1: The 2S1 Gvozdika is a light self-propelled howitzer armed with a 122 mm 2A18, and it fights differently from most vehicles around it by relying on high-explosive shells rather than armour-piercing rounds. Even when a shell fails to penetrate, the blast often cripples or destroys the target. Its light chassis gives an excellent top speed for reaching key positions early, but slow turret traverse, thin armour and a long reload mean a missed shot is usually fatal. It arrived in "Sons of Attila".
ussr_2s19_m1: Uraltransmash's 2S19M1 "Msta-S" succeeded the 2S3 with a far better howitzer and fire control; unveiled in 2000, it entered Russian service in 2007 and sold abroad, and its replacement, the 2S35, has been in production since 2015. In the game its autoloaded 152 mm can wreck almost any vehicle with HE or HEAT, uses APHEBC against lighter targets and even downs aircraft and helicopters with proximity-fused HE-VT. Armour and survivability are very poor, and a turret hit usually sets off the large autoloader rack, so it should fight from cover or distance and avoid close quarters, where slow traverse hurts. It arrived in "Hornet's Sting".
ussr_2s19_m2: The 2S19M2 "Msta-SM2", introduced in 2013, is Uraltransmash's improved Msta-S with an improved loading system and a new 152 mm gun; both versions remain in service. In the game this squadron vehicle reloads 1.5 seconds faster than the tech-tree 2S19M1, and its versatile ammunition handles most threats even against stronger opposition. It is still a glass cannon, with no more than 17 mm of armour and a huge autoloader in the turret, so it belongs behind cover or at range. Proximity-fused HE-VT rounds plus a roof 12.7 mm give it some anti-aircraft ability, but slow traverse makes close fights a bad idea. It arrived in "Hornet's Sting".
ussr_2s25: The 2S25 Sprut-SD continues the Soviet amphibious tank line begun with the PT-76B, using the light BMD-3 airborne chassis with hydropneumatic suspension and an odd-looking turret that carries a full 125 mm autoloaded gun, matching the T-72B's firepower. In the game it has an excellent power-to-weight ratio and reverses as fast as it drives forward, but its armour is extremely thin and its profile large. Without thermal sights it also struggles to find targets, so it works best by using its speed to ambush and then escape. It arrived in the "Direct Hit" update.
ussr_2s25m: The 2S25M Sprut-SDM1 modernises the Sprut-SD, moving to a reworked BMD-4M hull that shares its engine and gearbox with the BMP-3, rounding off the Soviet and Russian amphibious tank line. In the game it gives up much of the original's reverse speed and a little power, though it remains mobile. Its gains are in fire control, with thermal sights for gunner and commander fixing the 2S25's biggest flaw, and access to the potent 3BM60 APFSDS. It is routinely matched against Abrams and Leopard 2A4 tanks, which cancel out much of its speed advantage, so it needs even more caution. It arrived in "Ground Breaking".
ussr_2s38: Starting life on the BMP-3 as a technology demonstrator and then picked as a possible successor to the 2S6 Tunguska, the 2S38 carries a remotely operated 57 mm cannon and a tracking system for helicopters, low-flying aircraft and even rockets or missiles, with all three crew in the hull; as of 2020 it was entering service only slowly. In the game the fast-firing 57 mm with APFSDS and APHE threatens everything from jets to tanks, its APHE even piercing several IFVs and the Leopard 1 from the front, and it is deadly on flanks. Armour stops 14.5 mm fire all round but nothing heavier. It arrived in "Fire and Ice".
ussr_2s3m: The 2S3M Akatsiya was the first upgrade of the 2S3 howitzer, adding the 2A33 gun for better ammunition, range and accuracy and a single mechanised rack that lifted stowage to 46 rounds from 40; it became the main production model, fielded widely across the USSR and allied armies, and later led to the M1 and M2 upgrades. In the game it plays very differently from the SU casemate destroyers: it has a turret, very light armour and high mobility. Its HE and proximity-fused HE-VT shells can destroy even the heaviest tanks it meets, and the latter also damage low-flying aircraft. It arrived in "Winged Lions".
ussr_9a33bm3: The Osa ("wasp") mobile SAM system had a troubled birth, failing state trials in 1967 before entering Soviet service in 1971; the Osa-AKM of 1980 added the more agile 9M33M3 missile, guidance able to catch hovering and very low targets, a minimum range of about 1.5 km and better resistance to jamming. Exported to 25 countries, it remains in service. In the game it can hit manoeuvring aircraft out to 10 km and guide two missiles at one target, and its wheeled chassis lets it reposition unexpectedly. It is large and unarmoured, and its upward-angled missiles are almost useless against ground targets. It arrived in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
ussr_9a35_m2: The Strela-10M2 (NATO SA-13 Gopher) succeeded the Strela-1 as the short-range layer of Soviet army air defence, intended as a stopgap until the 2S6 arrived; poor results against contemporary jets in trials pushed deployment to the mid-1970s, and versions with improved seekers remain in use across former Soviet states. It was the first Soviet SAM vehicle in the game, added in "Apex Predators". It has no supporting search radar or command vehicle, so it works best hidden, waiting for jets or helicopters that stray too close. Its only other weapon is a PKM machine gun, so it should stay away from the front.
ussr_9p149: Fielded from the late 1970s, the Shturm-S used guided missiles to defeat well-protected NATO tanks from up to 5 km and able to fire from concealment, which suited it to defence; the later 9P149M added thermal sights and the 9M120 Ataka alongside the 9M114 Shturm, both available in-game through modifications. In the game it relies wholly on concealment, in contrast to the IT-1, and can strike ground and air targets as far as 7 km away. That reach outranges every helicopter it meets, letting it engage them comfortably. It arrived in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy".
ussr_9p157: KBM restarted work in 1996 on the 9M123 Khrizantema, an ATGM with laser and radar beam-riding versions intended for the Mi-28N and Ka-52; when those helicopters were delayed, a cheaper launcher on a modified BMP-3 chassis, the 9P157-2 Khrizantema-S, was devised and entered service in 2005. In the game this amphibious successor to the Shturm-S can guide missiles by radar as well as laser, and its 9M123 hits harder than any other Russian ATGM in the game, with a 1,200 mm tandem warhead and a 550 m/s flight speed. Weak armour and no gun make it a back-line sniper that relies on map knowledge and teammates. It arrived in "Starfighters".
ussr_a_12_mk_2_matilda_2A_F96: Britain sent 1,084 Matilda IIs to the Soviet Union under Lend-Lease between 1941 and 1943; judged weaker than the T-34 but better than the T-70 and T-60, they helped defend Moscow and later fought in Manchuria. A shortage of British ammunition and the lack of HE led to one tank being rearmed with a domestic ZiS-5 (F-96) 76 mm gun, but the conversion proved awkward and was dropped once supplies improved. In the game that gun and Soviet ammunition make it far more dangerous than the British original. Its thick, sloped armour defeats many shots, though top speed is only 24 km/h. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
ussr_asu_57: Built for the Soviet paratroop arm, the ASU-57 could be dropped from an An-12 with rocket-assisted parachutes and gave airborne forces their first workable armoured support, carrying a 57 mm Ch-51 gun derived from the ZiS-2 behind a thin welded aluminium hull; each airborne division had 54 before the ASU-85 replaced it from 1960. In the game it weighs just 3.3 tonnes and has almost no armour, so practically anything can kill it, and the open crew compartment is easy prey for aircraft. Its tiny size, though, lets it hide behind low cover for ambushes, ideally picking off isolated enemies singly. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
ussr_asu_85: Taking nearly ten years to develop because of the demands of air delivery, the ASU-85 used a modified, non-amphibious PT-76 chassis and began replacing the open ASU-57 with Soviet airborne forces in 1959; the BMD-1 superseded it from 1969, though some served in Afghanistan, and East Germany and Poland also used it. In the game it survives through stealth, as its thin roof leaves it badly exposed, especially to aircraft. The gun can handle almost any tank it meets, but it is less agile than the ASU-57, so it suits passive play on large maps with good ambush terrain and struggles in close-range city fights. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
ussr_ba_11: Meant as the BA-10's successor, the BA-11 was the sole heavy armoured car the Soviets produced, with better armour and a stronger engine, but flaws and technical problems made it a disappointment; production stopped with the 1941 invasion, a diesel version did not help, and combat claimed all 17 examples. In the game it is a strong flanker that plays much like the BT-5, and its crew layout lets it survive some hits away from the flat plates. Its thin roof cannot withstand even one strafing run, so keeping a low profile is vital. It was the Season 2 "Attack from the Sea" reward in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind".
ussr_bm_13n: The BM-13 "Katyusha" of 1938 traded accuracy and reload speed for the ability to drench a target quickly; doubted at first, it soon proved itself, and production passed 100,000 by the 1970s. The BM-13N, on the Lend-Lease Studebaker US6 chosen for its cross-country ability, was the version built in the largest numbers during the war, at around 1,800. In the game it is artillery, not a frontline fighter: the truck and two-man crew fall to stray machine-gun fire, and a dead zone of roughly 250 m ahead on flat ground means it must support allies from range. It was the 2017 Victory Day reward in Update 1.67 "Assault".
ussr_bm_31_12: A larger relative of the Katyusha, the BM-31 "Andryusha" of 1942 fired massive 300 mm rockets; demand for mobile siege artillery led to the truck-mounted BM-31-12 on the Lend-Lease Studebaker US6, which joined the fighting in June 1944 and helped smash German defences, with around 1,800 built. In the game, like the BM-13N, it is artillery on a fragile truck with two crew who can be knocked out by a glancing machine-gun burst. Its twelve rockets each carry almost 29 kg of explosive and destroy any vehicle they hit directly, but it cannot fire straight ahead and must keep its distance. It was the 2023 Legend of Victory event reward in "Sky Guardians".
ussr_bm_8_24: Developed from the BM-8-36 during the war, the BM-8-24 replaced the turret of T-60 and T-40 chassis with a launcher for M-8 rockets, adapted from the RS-82 aircraft rocket; the first reached the front in November 1941, 111 were built, and worn-out vehicles were withdrawn by spring 1943, their launchers moved onto trucks. In the game its rockets carry just 600 g of explosive and penetrate only 9 mm, so they cannot deal with armoured vehicles. They are effective only against unarmoured targets such as early anti-aircraft vehicles and SPGs. It arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm".
ussr_bmd_4: The post-Soviet BMD-4 put a Bakhcha-U turret carrying the BMP-3's 100 mm and 30 mm pairing on the improved BMD-3 airborne hull, giving remarkable firepower for its weight; accepted in 2004, it had only a short production run before economic problems halted it, later reviving as the BMD-4M. In the game it is lighter-armoured but more mobile than the BMP-3 and reloads its ATGMs faster. It is very quick in both directions and reaches flank or overwatch spots easily, but its front cannot even stop heavy machine guns, so it is best kept for ambushes on unaware enemies. It was a 2021 Summer Landing event reward in "Red Skies".
ussr_bmd_4m: Kurganmashzavod unveiled the BMD-4M in 2008 to fix the BMD-4's poor reliability, sharing many parts with the BMP-3 and adding a new engine and thermal sight while keeping the turret; cost and protection concerns nearly killed it, but renewed trials led to adoption in April 2016, and about 350 BMD-4s of all versions served by 2022. In the game it is an improved BMD-4 with more power and better armour, though it gives up the reverse gearbox. Small size and thermals suit scouting and quick deployment, but the gun sometimes lacks penetration and tank shells go straight through. It arrived in Update 2.43 "Storm Warning".
ussr_bmd_4m2: First shown publicly at Army-2017, the BMD-4M2 fits the BMD-4M with the BMP-3's turret, combining 100 mm and 30 mm guns with advanced fire control and increasing commonality between the two vehicles; it passed trials that year and is now in production and Russian service. In the game it pairs BMD-4M mobility with the BMP-3 turret, so its ATGMs reload more slowly than on other BMD-4s. Excellent agility and the ability to swim let it reach key positions early and outflank enemies, and thermal optics for the commander help it find targets in any conditions. It arrived in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
ussr_bmp_1: The Soviet BMP-1 of the 1960s was the first mass-produced infantry fighting vehicle and fought in conflicts from the Arab-Israeli wars to Chechnya; the late-1970s BMP-1P added better anti-tank capability, smoke launchers and more armour. In the game it suits shoot-and-scoot play, since being spotted usually means destruction: it snipes with ATGMs and saves the gun for close, unaware targets. The base version's manually steered missile comes with a 6-second gun autoloader unaffected by crew, while the BMP-1P modification brings smoke and a mouse-steered missile but loses the autoloader. It arrived in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
ussr_bmp_2: A late-1970s answer to the BMP-1's shortcomings, the BMP-2 brought better firepower, protection and fire control, with a 30 mm cannon, anti-tank missiles and amphibious ability; it became one of the world's most widespread IFVs, and upgrades such as the BMP-2M kept it in service for decades. In the game the 30 mm 2A42 handles helicopters as well as light vehicles and tanks, while 9M113 Konkurs missiles threaten tanks at range, making it a versatile support vehicle. Armour fails against anything above 12.7 mm and mobility trails some rivals, so positioning and teamwork matter. It arrived in Update 1.81 "The Valkyries".
ussr_bmp_2m: The BMP-2M, an early-2000s upgrade by the Instrument Design Bureau, fits the Berezhok turret, adding four Kornet launchers, an AG-30 grenade launcher, plus modern fire control with a gunner's thermal sight and commander's panoramic sight to the 30 mm 2A42; Algeria was its only customer until Russia joined in 2017. In the game tandem Kornets can kill almost anything head-on, a proximity-fused version tackles helicopters, and an APFSDS belt helps against tank sides. The thin armour fails against aircraft and flanking heavy machine guns, limited gun elevation hampers hilly maps, and some Western tanks can outpace it. It arrived in Update 1.99 "Starfighters".
ussr_bmp_3: Conceived at Kurganmashzavod in the 1970s and accepted by the Soviet Army in 1987, the BMP-3 was meant both to carry infantry and to provide heavy fire support, pairing a 100 mm 2A70 gun with a 30 mm 2A72 cannon in place of the BMP-2's 30 mm and Konkurs; it went on to Russian service and export. In the game, unlike earlier BMPs, it fires its ATGMs through the main gun, and the 100 mm can switch to HE for lighter targets with a faster reload than the missiles. Otherwise it keeps the strengths of earlier variants such as the BMP-2. It arrived in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack".
ussr_bmpt: Lessons from Afghanistan and Chechnya showed tanks needed a dedicated escort against infantry with ATGMs and RPGs, so the "Ramka" project got under way on a T-72A base in the mid-1980s; after 2006 trials it was produced on a T-90 base from 2011, first for Kazakhstan, though Russia only adopted it in 2017. In the game the "Terminator" carries two fast-firing 30 mm 2A42s, a quartet of 9M120-1 Ataka-T missiles, a pair of AG-30M grenade launchers and a fine thermal imager on a well-protected, mobile T-90 hull with five crew. Its drawbacks are few ATGMs, mediocre autocannon ammunition and slow reverse. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
ussr_bmpt_72: First displayed at Russia Arms Expo in 2013, the BMPT-72 "Terminator-2" converts existing T-72s into tank support vehicles, sharing more with the base tank than the first BMPT, cutting the crew from five to three and armouring the ATGM launchers to improve survivability and running costs; by 2022 only Algeria operated it, with three. In the game it differs from the standard BMPT in its T-72 hull, three-man crew and lack of grenade launchers, but gains stronger frontal armour, good thermals for gunner and commander and armoured Ataka-T launchers. Limited missiles, mediocre autocannon rounds and slow reverse remain weaknesses. It arrived in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
ussr_bt_5: The BT-5 belonged to the BT family of convertible tanks built on J. Walter Christie's idea: crews could take off the tracks and run on the road wheels at very high speed, sparing the fragile tracks of the 1930s. It added a larger cylindrical turret with a 45 mm 20-K and coaxial DT, but the convertible feature was of little use on Soviet roads and later designs dropped it. In the game its speed suits early objective grabs along roads or dashes to the map edge to hit enemies from the flank. Its thin armour means a penetrating hit almost always finishes it. It has been in the game since Update 1.45 "Steel Generals".
ussr_bt_7_1937: Developed from the BT-5 with the same 45 mm 20-K gun, the BT-7 had a welded, reshaped hull with frontal armour raised from 13 to 20 mm, a sloped turret, short-pitch tracks and the M-17T engine, a licensed BMW VI; it fought in the Winter and Continuation Wars and early in Barbarossa, and the survivors served on despite heavy losses after 1941. In the game it pairs a strong gun with a very mobile chassis but has no meaningful armour, so any hit is likely fatal. The best approach is to flank, fire into enemy sides, then relocate for the next ambush. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_bt_7_1937_td: Handed out to viewers of Enlisted broadcasts on Twitch and added with "Hot Tracks", the BT-7 TD matches the regular BT-7 in every respect except its unique paint, modelled on a BT that fought outside Moscow and resembling the scheme of the T-26 (1st Gv.T.Br.). The BT-7 itself refined the BT-5 with a welded hull, 20 mm frontal armour, a sloped turret and a licensed BMW VI engine, serving from the Winter War into the early years of Barbarossa. In the game a hard-hitting 45 mm on a fast chassis comes with almost no protection, so flanking shots followed by a quick move to a fresh ambush spot work best.
ussr_bt_7_m: The BT-7M kept the BT-7's welded hull, sloped turret and 45 mm 20-K but swapped the petrol engine for the V-2 diesel, gaining power, range and acceleration. In the game its 500 hp diesel makes it accelerate far faster than earlier BTs, so it can reach flanking spots or capture points quickly and escape trouble. Placed higher in the line-up, though, it meets many more enemies that can penetrate it easily, and the 45 mm struggles against tougher targets such as the M4A3 (105) or Matilda III. It arrived in "Ixwa Strike".
ussr_bt_7a_f32: Handed out as an Operation H.E.A.T. reward in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy", the BT-7A (F-32) shares the BT-7's hull, armour, powerplant and crew arrangement but mounts a new turret armed with a 76 mm F-32. In the game it is just as fast and fragile, and since almost everything it meets can penetrate it, stealth and speed matter even more than in the BT-7. The F-32's greater penetration and explosive filler let it take out bigger tanks with a single flank shot, and a pintle-mounted machine gun, rare on early Soviet tanks, adds a little anti-aircraft fire.
ussr_btr_152a: The first anti-aircraft version of the six-wheeled BTR-152, a Soviet APC built on ZIS-151 truck components from 1950 and the backbone of Soviet motor rifle units into the 1960s, the BTR-152A carries a pair of 14.5 mm KPVTs in a manually operated turret set inside the troop compartment, reloaded by other soldiers. In the game the two KPVTs do heavy damage to aircraft and can also wreck or damage certain light armoured vehicles. Mobile and hard-hitting, it is well suited to protecting teammates from air attack. It arrived in Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.".
ussr_btr_152d: The BTR-152D improves on the BTR-152A with a quadruple 14.5 mm KPVT mount, plus central tyre inflation, a winch at the front and night vision for the driver. In the game it handles much like its predecessor, but the doubled firepower makes downing aircraft far easier, and its armour-piercing rounds penetrate a fair amount of armour at close range. It is still lightly protected, so ground targets should not be its main focus. It arrived in "Kings of Battle".
ussr_btr_80a: The BTR series gave Soviet motor rifle units a cheaper, more numerous alternative to BMPs, progressing from the 8x8 BTR-60 through the BTR-70 to the diesel BTR-80, whose turret could elevate steeply for mountains and cities; a 1990s upgrade added the 30 mm 2A72 in a new BPPU turret, creating the BTR-80A. In the game its autocannon can shred medium tanks from ambush, but it is as big as a BMP and its wheels limit cross-country movement, making hiding places harder to find outside towns. Its APDS reaches well, so watching enemy routes from afar and raking their sides works best. It arrived in "La Royale".
ussr_btr_82at: The BTR-80A's crude fire control left it unable to shoot well while moving or in darkness, so the BTR-82A added a stabiliser and a stronger engine; the BTR-82AT, shown at Army-2019 and built from 2021, added a laser rangefinder, thermal sight and slat armour against HEAT. In the game it beats the BTR-80A in every major respect: the stabiliser makes flanking fire on the move effective, thermals allow long-range ATGM shots, and mobility improves. Base armour is unchanged, and the slat armour stops heavy machine guns but slows it more than the engine can offset. It arrived in Update 2.51 "Spearhead".
ussr_btr_zd: Designed late in the 1970s and fielded in 1984, the BTR-ZD gave Soviet airborne troops a mobile carrier for Strela and Igla MANPADS; paratroopers later mounted a twin 23 mm ZU-23 on the BTR-D-based vehicle, an idea the factory adopted along with shields to protect the gunners from fragments and rifle fire, and it remains with the Russian VDV. In the game its twin 23 mm cannons are accurate and fast-firing, and the BMD-1-derived chassis is mobile, but crew protection is minimal. The guns work best at short range, so it pays to wait for enemies to come close. It arrived in "Danger Zone".
ussr_buk_m3_fcs: The Buk family replaced the 2K12 Kub, giving each launcher a dedicated fire-control radar after Kub combat experience; the M1 followed in 1983 and the M2, with the longer-ranged 9M317, in 1998, while the 2016 Buk-M3 raised each launcher's load from four missiles to six and reacts faster. In the game the system outranges the Pantsir-S1, its missiles are faster and more agile, and it can engage up to 12 targets. Nothing within 2.5 km can be intercepted, though, leaving it exposed to aircraft that pop up for a strafing pass and to Brimstone or Maverick attacks, so it complements the Pantsir as a long-range layer. It arrived in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
ussr_buk_m3_launcher: The Buk-M3 of 2016 is the latest of a SAM family that replaced the Kub; its launchers carry six missiles instead of four and each has its own tracking radar, letting them fire and guide missiles without the radar vehicle at reduced performance. In the game this TELAR holds six 9M317MA missiles, plus six more via the ammunition crate mechanic, which reach 1,550 m/s and 70 km, pull hard, carry large warheads and combine active radar homing with inertial guidance and datalink. Its own radar can steer six missiles at once and covers 60 degrees vertically, but it has no IFF. It arrived in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force".
ussr_garford_putilov: Built for the Imperial Russian Army in 1915-16 on an imported Garford five-ton lorry chassis, the Garford-Putilov was unusual for its time in carrying a Model 1910 76.2 mm field gun alongside three Maxim machine guns, for use against fortifications; 48 were made, proving mechanically reliable but overweight and poor off-road. In the game it is slow and barely proof against small-calibre machine guns. With only low-velocity HE and shrapnel shells, it can hurt only thin-skinned targets such as its contemporaries and unarmoured AA, so it is a support vehicle at best. It was a reward in the 2025 "The Great War!" event in "Hornet's Sting".
ussr_gaz_4m: When Germany invaded, the Soviet Union was short of anti-aircraft guns, and the GAZ-AAA (4M), developed in 1938, filled part of the gap by grouping four 7.62 mm Maxims, left over from Imperial stocks, on a GAZ-AAA lorry; delivered in late 1941, it was later replaced by the DShK-armed version, and little else is documented about it. In the game it is light and nimble and keeps early aircraft such as biplanes at bay, and its large ammunition supply allows generous bursts. Its guns cannot penetrate other vehicles, so it should stay out of ground fights. It arrived in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory".
ussr_gaz_dshk: The second anti-aircraft version of the GAZ-AAA truck swaps the quad Maxim of the 4M for one DShK 12.7 mm, adding hitting power against aircraft and light vehicles. In the game the platform is just as agile and unprotected, but each hit does more damage to aircraft, and the DShK can also kill the lightly armoured vehicles common at its level. Penetration is still modest and there is no protection, so it should avoid charging into fights and instead rely on ambushes and quick raids. It arrived in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
ussr_gaz_mm_72k: Trials in late 1941 mounting the 72-K 25 mm gun on a GAZ-MM's cargo bed went well, and series production followed at Kolomna's locomotive plant, helped by the fact that it avoided the gun's hard-to-make standard mount; about 200 were built before the factory was evacuated that December. In the game the 25 mm fires quickly and reloads fast, and its HE incendiary shells are very effective against aircraft. Excellent mobility helps it escape enemy fire, but it has almost no armour, so rifle-calibre bullets or nearby fragments can knock out the crew. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_is_1: Designed to fix the KV series' shortcomings in firepower and protection without exceeding the KV-85's weight, the IS-1 combined a new well-sloped hull with the KV-85's three-man turret and 85 mm D-5T gun and a 520 hp V2-IS diesel; built at the Chelyabinsk Kirov Plant from October 1943, it was replaced by the superior IS-2 in January 1944 after only about 200 were made. In the game its hull protection improves on the KV-85, the sloped front shedding many shells at range, though the lower front plate is vulnerable to nearly everything it meets. KV-85 players will find it familiar. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_is_1_kit_3rank: The IS-1, derived from the experimental KV-13, carried an 85 mm gun and was produced only between late 1943 and early 1944 before the 122 mm IS-2 replaced it; IS tanks served as breakthrough tanks in 1944-45, especially in city assaults. The IS-1 ('45) is a composite of late-war Soviet tanks, with Berlin-operation recognition stripes, five kill marks on the barrel, camouflage netting, boxes and crew kit. In the game decent mobility lets it join attacks with its quick-firing 85 mm, and the hull, reinforced with track links, resists many shells. The turret is far weaker, and the cramped crew layout means the first hit can be fatal. It arrived in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
ussr_is_2_1943: Rushed into service as the Soviet answer to the Panther and Tiger, the IS-2 combined the IS-1's blended, sloped hull front, proof against German 88 mm AP at 1,000 m, with a huge 122 mm D-25T firing heavy two-piece rounds; a cramped turret limited the crew to four, and about 2,252 were delivered in 1944. In the game its protection matches the IS-1, but the 122 mm can destroy virtually any vehicle in one hit. The reload often exceeds 20 seconds, so it should avoid fighting several enemies at once. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_is_2_1944: The 1944 model of the IS-2 replaced the stepped hull front with a single 100 mm glacis sloped at 60 degrees, added a roof DShK for air defence and proved far more reliable; around 1,150 were built before the IS-3 took over in May 1945. In the game the smooth glacis makes ricochets more likely than penetrations, and the 122 mm D-25T still kills almost anything in one shot, though the slow reload means each round must count. Decent reverse speed even makes it practical to fight with the engine deck towards the enemy, and researchable mesh screens help against some HEAT. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_is_2_1944_321: The 1944 model of the IS-2 replaced the stepped 120 mm front with a single 100 mm plate at 60 degrees, moved the driver's vision slit aside and added a DShK by the commander's cupola. No.321 represents the battle-worn IS-2s that fought through Berlin, helping take the city despite around 60 losses. In the game it matches the IS-2 (1944) minus mudguards and mesh armour: the 122 mm D-25T usually kills with one hit or overpressure, and the DShK handles aircraft and light vehicles, but the long reload and exposed muzzle brake favour play just behind the front. It was a Legend of Victory reward in "Wind of Change".
ussr_is_2_1944_revenge: This IS-2 carries the inscription "Revenge for the Hero Brother", carved by Mikhail Krasikov after his younger brother Nikolay, a tank commander honoured as a Hero of the Soviet Union for actions around Kiev, Lyutezh and Vyshgorod, was killed near Vinnitsa in November 1943; Mikhail later fought with it in Pomerania. In the game it is an IS-2 (1944) without the optional mesh screens: the sloped glacis protects well and the 122 mm D-25T kills in one shot, but the slow reload demands careful aim. Sold as a pack from Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it has since come and gone from sale several times.
ussr_is_2m_kit_4rank: By the 1950s many IS-2 components were worn out or obsolete, so from 1957 the tanks were overhauled as the IS-2M, receiving a fresh powerplant and gearbox, 35 rounds of ammunition, a driver's periscope, turret changes, a new elevation mechanism and radio; moved to reserve from the 1960s, examples went to Czechoslovakia, North Korea and Cuba, Russia retired its last in 1993, and Cuba still uses them as pillboxes. In the game the IS-2M (Be Prepared!) behaves almost exactly like the IS-2, with a powerful 122 mm gun and heavy armour but a very long reload and unimpressive mobility. It arrived in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
ussr_is_3: The IS-3 introduced the pointed "pike nose" hull and rounded turret that shaped later Soviet tanks; the first three were completed in May 1945, too late for the war in Europe, and it served through the Cold War until heavy tanks gave way to main battle tanks. In the game its 122 mm D-25T hits extremely hard, especially with BR-471D, and the 110 mm pike nose and thick, well-angled turret make it a frontal brawler. It turns and accelerates slowly, its sides are weak and flankers are dangerous, but strong reverse helps it escape. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_is_4m: Meant, like the IS-3, to succeed the IS-2, the 53-tonne IS-4 had extremely thick armour and a 750 hp diesel but kept the D-25T 122 mm, offering little over the lighter, cheaper IS-3; it was built from 1947 until work on tanks over 50 tonnes stopped in 1949, and 25 improved IS-4Ms followed in 1951. In the game its armour is even tougher than the IS-3's and nearly impossible to penetrate frontally with conventional rounds, especially at a slight angle. The 122 mm can feel inadequate at its level, and the weight makes it sluggish in fast battles. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_is_6: Developed in secret alongside the IS-4 as a late-war successor to the IS-2, the IS-6 looked superior on paper to any German tank but suffered mechanical faults and poor performance, losing to the IS-4 in trials; a final improvement attempt, the Object 252U, achieved little. In the game few tanks at its level are more dreaded: a strong gun sits behind steep, heavy armour that defeats most conventional rounds, and it moves better than other IS tanks. Good reverse speed and agility let it handle difficult terrain and fit almost any role. It arrived in Update 1.67 "Assault".
ussr_is_7: Designed by Nikolai Shashmurin in Leningrad from 1945, the 68-tonne IS-7 was the largest IS tank, with a 150 mm pike nose and a naval-derived 130 mm S-70 fed by a conveyor loader; too heavy and costly, it lost out to the T-10 and was cancelled in 1949. In the game almost nothing conventional penetrates its front, its sides are far thicker than earlier IS tanks', and it can reload in around 10 seconds. Eight machine guns deter light vehicles and a strong engine gives good mobility for breakthroughs, though very large-calibre guns can still cripple it. It was the 2018 Operation S.U.M.M.E.R. reward in Update 1.79 "Project X".
ussr_isu_122: After the ISU-152, engineers fitted the 122 mm A-19S to the IS chassis as Object 242; testing went well, but mass production only began in early 1944, when spare IS chassis were ordered to receive the gun. The ISU-122 was used mainly against tanks. In the game it is a long-range sniper with accurate, deep-penetrating shells and a reasonable reverse gear. It should fire from concealment and keep enemies away from objectives at distance, staying off the front line because its height and thin front plate leave it exposed to flanking or swarming. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_isu_122s: An upgraded build of the ISU-122 rather than a new variant, the ISU-122S gave its gun a semi-automatic breech, creating the 122 mm D-25S and doubling the rate of fire to 3 rounds a minute; its rounded mantlet and two-chamber muzzle brake identify it, and German reports called it Type 249. In the game it remains a long-range sniper with strong penetration, good accuracy and decent reverse speed, best kept hidden away from the front because of its tall profile and weak front. The reload is better but still slower than most enemies', so a miss rarely gets a second chance. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_isu_152: The ISU-152 carried the SU-152's 152 mm ML-20S howitzer on the IS heavy tank chassis, aimed by turning the whole vehicle, and served mostly as mobile artillery supporting infantry and armoured attacks, remaining in use with several countries into the 1970s. In the game most opponents at its level are heavily armoured, so armour-piercing shells are usually the best choice, with HE still useful against lighter vehicles. The reload is extremely long, so every shot must count, and although its armour improves on the SU-152, it is not something to rely on. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
ussr_it_1: Built in the 1960s on the T-62 chassis, the IT-1 fired the purpose-made 3M7 Drakon ATGM, reaching 3 km and penetrating 500 mm under radio command guidance; bulky, complex guidance gear and a large dead zone from the missile's minimum range made it unpopular, and it was retired after five years. In the game it was among the earliest missile carriers added, with a low turret whose roof launcher is its only weapon. It is fragile, so it works best at long range behind cover, but the missiles are slow to arrive and alert enemies can shoot them down. It arrived in Update 1.59 "Flaming Arrows".
ussr_kv_122: Proposed late in the war, the KV-122 would have rearmed the KV-85 with copies of the IS-2's turret and 122 mm gun so it could take on late-war German heavy tanks; only one prototype was built, since attention had already moved to the IS-2, recalling the few KV-85s for conversion seemed pointless, and resources, transport and trained crews were scarce. In the game the IS-2 turret and gun are the obvious change, while the engine is the 520 hp V-2IS rather than the 600 hp V-2K of most KVs. In effect it is an IS-2 that faces easier opposition. It arrived in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters".
ussr_kv_1_L_11: Developed in 1938-39 by teams under A. S. Ermolaev and then N. L. Dukhov, the KV-1 was among the best-protected tanks of the early war; the first production model, armed with the 76 mm L-11, was built from February 1940 to early 1941, 144 in all, and fought in the Winter War and against Germany, halting several advances. In the game its all-round armour shrugs off most opposing guns, especially when angled. BR-350A APCBC penetrates modestly but its filler does heavy damage after penetration. The long reload and slow turret make close fights awkward, and mobility is mediocre. It has been in the game since the ground forces closed beta.
